设内层连分式为

\[
x_n=\alpha_1+\cfrac1{\alpha_2+\cfrac1{\alpha_3+\cdots+\cfrac1{\alpha_n}}},
\]

则

\[
b_n=1+\frac1{x_n}.
\]

函数 \(f(x)=1+\frac1x\) 在 \(x>0\) 上严格递减，所以比较 \(b_i,b_j\) 的大小等价于反向比较 \(x_i,x_j\) 的大小。

下面判断 \(x_n\) 的单调规律。

固定 \(m\)，令

\[
F_m(t)=[\alpha_1;\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_{m-1},t].
\]

当 \(n\ge m\) 时，

\[
x_n=F_m\bigl([\alpha_m;\alpha_{m+1},\ldots,\alpha_n]\bigr).
\]

若 \(n>m\)，则

\[
[\alpha_m;\alpha_{m+1},\ldots,\alpha_n]=\alpha_m+\text{正数}>\alpha_m.
\]

再看 \(F_m(t)\) 的单调性：

- \(F_1(t)=t\)，递增；
- 而

\[
F_m(t)=F_{m-1}\left(\alpha_{m-1}+\frac1t\right),
\]

其中 \(t\mapsto \alpha_{m-1}+\frac1t\) 递减，因此每增加一层，单调性翻转一次。

所以：

\[
F_m(t) \text{ 在 } m \text{ 为奇数时递增，在 } m \text{ 为偶数时递减。}
\]

于是当 \(m<n\) 时：

- 若 \(m\) 为奇数，则 \(x_n>x_m\)，从而 \(b_n<b_m\)；
- 若 \(m\) 为偶数，则 \(x_n<x_m\)，从而 \(b_n>b_m\)。

逐项判断：

- (A) \(b_1<b_5\)：\(1\) 是奇数，应有 \(b_5<b_1\)，错误；
- (B) \(b_3<b_8\)：\(3\) 是奇数，应有 \(b_8<b_3\)，错误；
- (C) \(b_6<b_2\)：\(2\) 是偶数，应有 \(b_6>b_2\)，错误；
- (D) \(b_4<b_7\)：\(4\) 是偶数，应有 \(b_7>b_4\)，正确。

\[

\[

其中 \(S\) 是底面四边形面积。

设三场比赛按顺序进行的对手对应的获胜概率分别为 \(a,b,c\)，其中 \(\{a,b,c\}=\{p_1,p_2,p_3\}\)，第二场获胜概率为 \(b\)。

“连胜两盘”即第一场和第二场都赢，或第二场和第三场都赢。设事件：

- \(A\)：前两场都赢；
- \(B\)：后两场都赢。

则

\[
p=P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(AB)
\]

由独立性：

\[
P(A)=ab,\qquad P(B)=bc,\qquad P(AB)=abc
\]

所以

\[
p=ab+bc-abc=b(a+c-ac)
\]

分别讨论第二场对手：

1. 第二场对甲，则 \(b=p_1\)：

\[
p_1=p_1(p_2+p_3-p_2p_3)
\]

2. 第二场对乙，则 \(b=p_2\)：

\[
p_2=p_2(p_1+p_3-p_1p_3)
\]

3. 第二场对丙，则 \(b=p_3\)：

\[
p_3=p_3(p_1+p_2-p_1p_2)
\]

比较大小：

\[
\begin{aligned}
p_2-p_1
&=p_2(p_1+p_3-p_1p_3)-p_1(p_2+p_3-p_2p_3)\\
&=p_2p_3-p_1p_3\\
&=p_3(p_2-p_1)>0
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
p_3-p_2
&=p_3(p_1+p_2-p_1p_2)-p_2(p_1+p_3-p_1p_3)\\
&=p_1p_3-p_1p_2\\
&=p_1(p_3-p_2)>0
\end{aligned}
\]

因此

\[
p_3>p_2>p_1
\]

即第二场对丙时，连胜两盘的概率最大。

答案是D

=

解：

\(\triangle ABC\) 的底 \(AB=2\)，高为 \(1\)，所以面积为

\[
S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac12\cdot 2\cdot 1=1.
\]

直线将其平分，则它截出的某一顶点处的小三角形面积必须为 \(\frac12\)。

因为斜率 \(a>0\) 且为有限值，分三种情况讨论直线与三角形两边的交点。

---

### 1. 直线交 \(AB,AC\)，截去 \(A\) 角

设

\[
\frac{AP}{AB}=r,\qquad \frac{AQ}{AC}=s.
\]

则小三角形面积为

\[
rs\cdot S_{\triangle ABC}=rs=\frac12.
\]

坐标可写为

\[
P=(-1+2r,0),\qquad Q=(-1+s,s).
\]

斜率为

\[
a=\frac{s-0}{(-1+s)-(-1+2r)}
=\frac{s}{s-2r}.
\]

由 \(rs=\frac12\) 得 \(2r=\frac1s\)，于是

\[
a=\frac{s}{s-\frac1s}
=\frac{s^2}{s^2-1}.
\]

由于 \(0<s\le 1\)，当 \(s<1\) 时 \(a<0\)；当 \(s=1\) 时直线为竖直线 \(x=0\)，不能写成有限斜率的 \(y=ax+b\)。  
所以这种情况不可能。

---

### 2. 直线交 \(AB,BC\)，截去 \(B\) 角

设

\[
\frac{BP}{BA}=r,\qquad \frac{BQ}{BC}=s.
\]

同样有

\[
rs=\frac12.
\]

坐标为

\[
P=(1-2r,0),\qquad Q=(1-s,s).
\]

斜率

\[
a=\frac{s}{(1-s)-(1-2r)}
=\frac{s}{2r-s}.
\]

由 \(r=\frac1{2s}\)，得

\[
a=\frac{s}{\frac1s-s}
=\frac{s^2}{1-s^2}.
\]

要 \(a>0\) 且有限，需要 \(0<s<1\)。又 \(r\le 1\)，即

\[
\frac1{2s}\le 1\Rightarrow s\ge \frac12.
\]

所以

\[
s\in\left[\frac12,1\right).
\]

截距 \(b\) 满足

\[
b=-a(1-2r).
\]

代入 \(2r=\frac1s\)，得

\[
b=\frac{s}{1+s}.
\]

当 \(s\in\left[\frac12,1\right)\) 时，

\[
b\in\left[\frac13,\frac12\right).
\]

其中 \(s=1\) 对应竖直线 \(x=0\)，不能取，所以 \(\frac12\) 不包含。

---

### 3. 直线交 \(AC,BC\)，截去 \(C\) 角

设

\[
\frac{CP}{CA}=r,\qquad \frac{CQ}{CB}=s.
\]

则

\[
rs=\frac12.
\]

坐标为

\[
P=(-r,1-r),\qquad Q=(s,1-s).
\]

斜率

\[
a=\frac{(1-s)-(1-r)}{s-(-r)}
=\frac{r-s}{r+s}.
\]

要 \(a>0\)，需 \(r>s\)。由 \(r=\frac1{2s}\)，得

\[
\frac1{2s}>s\Rightarrow s<\frac1{\sqrt2}.
\]

又 \(r\le 1\)，即

\[
\frac1{2s}\le 1\Rightarrow s\ge \frac12.
\]

所以

\[
s\in\left[\frac12,\frac1{\sqrt2}\right).
\]

截距

\[
b=(1-s)-as
=\frac{r+s-2rs}{r+s}.
\]

因为 \(rs=\frac12\)，所以

\[
b=\frac{r+s-1}{r+s}.
\]

代入 \(r=\frac1{2s}\)，可得

\[
b=1-\frac{2s}{1+2s^2}.
\]

当 \(s\) 从 \(\frac12\) 增大到 \(\frac1{\sqrt2}\) 时，\(b\) 从 \(\frac13\) 减小到

\[
1-\frac1{\sqrt2}=1-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}.
\]

其中 \(s=\frac1{\sqrt2}\) 对应 \(a=0\)，不符合 \(a>0\)，所以下端点不包含。

因此这种情况给出

\[
b\in\left(1-\frac{\sqrt2}{2},\frac13\right].
\]

---

合并第 2、3 种情况：

\[
b\in\left[\frac13,\frac12\right)\cup\left(1-\frac{\sqrt2}{2},\frac13\right]
=\left(1-\frac{\sqrt2}{2},\frac12\right).
\]

对应选项为 B。

答案是B

设球的半径为 \(R\)。

由球的体积：

\[

\]

得

\[
R^3=8 \Rightarrow R=2
\]

设球心到公共底面（球的同一截面）所在平面的距离为 \(d\)，则截面圆半径 \(r\) 满足：

\[
r^2=R^2-d^2
\]

两个圆锥共用该截面作为底面，顶点在球面上，因此它们的高分别为该截面到球面两侧的距离：

\[
h_1=R-d,\qquad h_2=R+d
\]

已知两个圆锥的高之比为 \(1:3\)，所以

\[
\frac{R-d}{R+d}=\frac{1}{3}
\]

\[
3(R-d)=R+d
\]

\[
3R-3d=R+d
\]

\[
2R=4d
\]

\[
d=\frac{R}{2}=1
\]

于是底面圆半径平方：

\[
r^2=R^2-d^2=2^2-1^2=3
\]

两个圆锥体积之和为：

\[
V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2(h_1+h_2)
\]

而

\[
h_1+h_2=(R-d)+(R+d)=2R=4
\]

所以

\[
V=\frac{1}{3}\pi\cdot 3\cdot 4=4\pi
\]

答案是B

先分别分析两段函数的零点。

---

## 1. 当 \(x<a\) 时

\[
f(x)=\cos(2\pi x-2\pi a)=\cos(2\pi(x-a))
\]

零点满足

\[
2\pi(x-a)=\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi
\]

即

\[
x-a=\frac{2k+1}{4}
\]

由于这里要求 \(x<a\)，所以取负奇数项：

\[
x=a-\frac{2m-1}{4},\qquad m=1,2,3,\dots
\]

又因为零点必须在 \((0,+\infty)\) 内，所以

\[
0<a-\frac{2m-1}{4}<a
\]

等价于

\[
0<2m-1<4a
\]

因此左段零点的个数为

\[
N_1(a)=\#\{ \text{正奇数 } q: q<4a\}
\]

---

## 2. 当 \(x\ge a\) 时

\[
f(x)=x^2-2(a+1)x+a^2+5
\]

其判别式为

\[
\Delta=4(a+1)^2-4(a^2+5)=8a-16=8(a-2)
\]

所以：

- 若 \(a<2\)，右段无实根；
- 若 \(a=2\)，右段有重根；
- 若 \(a>2\)，右段有两个实根。

先排除 \(a<2\)。  
若 \(a<2\)，则 \(4a<8\)，左段零点最多为

\[
q=1,3,5,7
\]

共 4 个，右段无零点，总数不可能达到 6。  
若 \(a=2\)，左段零点为 4 个，右段重根 \(x=3\) 计 1 个零点，共 5 个。

因此必须有

\[
a>2
\]

当 \(a>2\) 时，右段两根为

\[
x_{1,2}=a+1\pm\sqrt{2a-4}
\]

其中

\[
x_2=a+1+\sqrt{2a-4}>a
\]

恒在右段定义域内。

而

\[
x_1=a+1-\sqrt{2a-4}\ge a
\]

等价于

\[
1\ge \sqrt{2a-4}
\]

即

\[
a\le \frac52
\]

所以右段零点数：

\[
N_2(a)=
\begin{cases}
2, & 2<a\le \dfrac52,\\[4pt]
1, & a>\dfrac52.
\end{cases}
\]

---

## 3. 左段零点个数

因为 \(a>2\)，所以 \(4a>8\)。

左段零点数取决于正奇数 \(q<4a\) 的个数。

### 当左段有 4 个零点时

需要

\[
7<4a\le 9
\]

即

\[
\frac74<a\le \frac94
\]

结合 \(a>2\)，得

\[
a\in\left(2,\frac94\right]
\]

### 当左段有 5 个零点时

需要

\[
9<4a\le 11
\]

即

\[
\frac94<a\le \frac{11}4
\]

---

## 4. 合计恰有 6 个零点

### 情形一：\(2<a\le \dfrac52\)

此时右段有 2 个零点，需要左段有 4 个零点：

\[
a\in\left(2,\frac94\right]
\]

### 情形二：\(a>\dfrac52\)

此时右段有 1 个零点，需要左段有 5 个零点：

\[
a\in\left(\frac94,\frac{11}4\right]
\]

再与 \(a>\dfrac52\) 取交集，得

\[
a\in\left(\frac52,\frac{11}4\right]
\]

---

综上，

\[
a\in\left(2,\frac94\right]\cup\left(\frac52,\frac{11}4\right]
\]

解：

两平面平行 \(\alpha//\beta\) 表示两平面没有公共点。

**选项 B 是充要条件：**

- **必要性**：若 \(\alpha//\beta\)，则 \(\alpha\) 与 \(\beta\) 无公共点。于是 \(\alpha\) 内任一条直线都与 \(\beta\) 无公共点，即都与 \(\beta\) 平行。因此在 \(\alpha\) 内可取两条相交直线，它们都与 \(\beta\) 平行。

- **充分性**：若 \(\alpha\) 内有两条相交直线都与 \(\beta\) 平行。若 \(\alpha\) 与 \(\beta\) 相交，设交线为 \(l\)。在平面 \(\alpha\) 内，一条与 \(\beta\) 无公共点的直线不能与交线 \(l\) 相交，只能与 \(l\) 平行。于是这两条相交直线都应平行于 \(l\)，从而它们互相平行，不可能相交，矛盾。所以 \(\alpha\) 与 \(\beta\) 不相交，即 \(\alpha//\beta\)。

其他选项都不是充要条件：

- A：两平面相交时，一个平面内也有无数条直线与另一平面平行，例如与交线平行的直线。
- C：两个相交平面也可能同时平行于同一条直线，例如都平行于它们的交线。
- D：两个相交平面也可以同时垂直于同一平面，例如两个竖直平面都垂直于水平面。

样本空间为两次取球的所有有序结果，共 \(6\times 6=36\) 种。

设：

- 甲：\(A=\{第一次为1\}\)，则  
  \[
  P(A)=\frac{6}{36}=\frac16
  \]

- 乙：\(B=\{第二次为2\}\)，则  
  \[
  P(B)=\frac{6}{36}=\frac16
  \]

- 丙：\(C=\{两次数字之和为8\}\)。  
  满足的有序对为：
  \[
  (2,6),(3,5),(4,4),(5,3),(6,2)
  \]
  共 5 种，所以  
  \[
  P(C)=\frac{5}{36}
  \]

- 丁：\(D=\{两次数字之和为7\}\)。  
  满足的有序对为：
  \[
  (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1)
  \]
  共 6 种，所以  
  \[
  P(D)=\frac{6}{36}=\frac16
  \]

逐项判断：

### (A) 甲与丙是否独立？

\[
P(A\cap C)
\]

第一次为 1，且两次和为 8，则第二次必须为 7，不可能。

\[
P(A\cap C)=0
\]

但

\[
P(A)P(C)=\frac16\cdot\frac{5}{36}=\frac{5}{216}\neq 0
\]

所以甲与丙不独立。

---

### (B) 甲与丁是否独立？

\[
P(A\cap D)
\]

第一次为 1，且两次和为 7，则第二次必须为 6，只有一种：

\[
(1,6)
\]

所以

\[
P(A\cap D)=\frac1{36}
\]

又

\[
P(A)P(D)=\frac16\cdot\frac16=\frac1{36}
\]

相等，所以甲与丁独立。

---

### (C) 乙与丙是否独立？

\[
P(B\cap C)
\]

第二次为 2，且两次和为 8，则第一次必须为 6，只有一种：

\[
(6,2)
\]

所以

\[
P(B\cap C)=\frac1{36}
\]

但

\[
P(B)P(C)=\frac16\cdot\frac{5}{36}=\frac{5}{216}\neq \frac1{36}
\]

所以乙与丙不独立。

---

### (D) 丙与丁是否独立？

丙表示和为 8，丁表示和为 7，二者不可能同时发生。

\[
P(C\cap D)=0
\]

但

\[
P(C)P(D)=\frac{5}{36}\cdot\frac16=\frac{5}{216}\neq 0
\]

所以丙与丁不独立。

因此只有 (B) 正确。

设命题  
\(P\)：存在 \(k\in\mathbb Z\)，使得 \(\alpha=k\pi+(-1)^k\beta\)；  
\(Q\)：\(\sin\alpha=\sin\beta\)。

**1. 证明 \(P\Rightarrow Q\)**

若存在 \(k\in\mathbb Z\)，使  
\[
\alpha=k\pi+(-1)^k\beta
\]

分两种情况：

- 若 \(k\) 为偶数，设 \(k=2m\)，则  
  \[
  \alpha=2m\pi+\beta
  \]
  所以  
  \[
  \sin\alpha=\sin(2m\pi+\beta)=\sin\beta
  \]

- 若 \(k\) 为奇数，设 \(k=2m+1\)，则  
  \[
  \alpha=(2m+1)\pi-\beta
  \]
  所以  
  \[
  \sin\alpha=\sin((2m+1)\pi-\beta)=\sin(\pi-\beta)=\sin\beta
  \]

因此 \(P\Rightarrow Q\)。

---

**2. 证明 \(Q\Rightarrow P\)**

若  
\[
\sin\alpha=\sin\beta
\]

则  
\[
\sin\alpha-\sin\beta=0
\]
利用和差化积：
\[
2\cos\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}\sin\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}=0
\]

所以有两种情况：

**情况一：**
\[
\sin\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}=0
\]
则  
\[
\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}=m\pi
\]
即  
\[
\alpha=\beta+2m\pi
\]
取 \(k=2m\)，则 \((-1)^k=1\)，有  
\[
\alpha=k\pi+(-1)^k\beta
\]

**情况二：**
\[
\cos\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}=0
\]
则  
\[
\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}+m\pi
\]
即  
\[
\alpha+\beta=(2m+1)\pi
\]
所以  
\[
\alpha=(2m+1)\pi-\beta
\]
取 \(k=2m+1\)，则 \((-1)^k=-1\)，有  
\[
\alpha=k\pi+(-1)^k\beta
\]

因此 \(Q\Rightarrow P\)。

---

综上，\(P\) 与 \(Q\) 等价，所以原命题是“\(\sin\alpha=\sin\beta\)”的充分必要条件。

答案是C

\[
a^c>b^c
\]

### 选项 B：\(ab^c<ba^c\)

比较两边比值：

\[
\frac{ab^c}{ba^c}
=\frac{a}{b}\cdot \left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^c
=\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^{1-c}
\]

由于 \(a>b>1\)，所以 \(\frac{a}{b}>1\)；又 \(0<c<1\)，所以 \(1-c>0\)。  
因此

\[
\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^{1-c}>1
\]

即

\[
ab^c>ba^c
\]

所以 B 错误。

---

### 选项 C：\(a\log_b c<b\log_a c\)

用自然对数表示：

\[
a\log_b c=a\cdot \frac{\ln c}{\ln b},\qquad
b\log_a c=b\cdot \frac{\ln c}{\ln a}
\]

因为 \(0<c<1\)，所以 \(\ln c<0\)。  
设 \(-\ln c=m>0\)，则原不等式等价于

\[
-\frac{am}{\ln b}<-\frac{bm}{\ln a}
\]

两边同乘 \(-1\)，不等号方向改变：

\[
\frac{a}{\ln b}>\frac{b}{\ln a}
\]

由于 \(\ln a>0,\ln b>0\)，交叉相乘得：

\[
a\ln a>b\ln b
\]

\[
f'(x)=\ln x+1>0\quad (x>1)
\]

又 \(a>b>1\)，所以

\[
a\ln a>b\ln b
\]

成立，因此 C 正确。

\log_b c=\frac{\ln c}{\ln b}

因为 \(\ln c<0\)，且 \(a>b>1\)，所以 \(\ln a>\ln b>0\)。

\]

由于 \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\) 是对称轴，所以它也是一个极值点。正弦函数相邻极值点横坐标相距半个周期：
\[

\]
Hence
\[
f(f(x))-x
= -\lambda^3x^4+2\lambda^3x^3-\lambda^2(\lambda+1)x^2+(\lambda^2-1)x.
\]
Factoring gives
\[
f(f(x))-x
=
-\lambda^2x(\lambda x-\lambda+1)
\left(
x^2-\frac{\lambda+1}{\lambda}x+\frac{\lambda+1}{\lambda^2}
\right).
\]

The fixed points of \(f\) are the roots of
\[
f(x)-x=0
\iff
-x(\lambda x-\lambda+1)=0,
\]
so they are \(x=0\) and \(x=\frac{\lambda-1}{\lambda}\). Therefore any solution with \(f(x)\ne x\) must satisfy the quadratic
\[
x^2-\frac{\lambda+1}{\lambda}x+\frac{\lambda+1}{\lambda^2}=0.
\]

Its discriminant is
\[
\Delta
=
\left(\frac{\lambda+1}{\lambda}\right)^2
-4\frac{\lambda+1}{\lambda^2}
=
\frac{(\lambda+1)(\lambda-3)}{\lambda^2}.
\]
Since \(\lambda>0\), real roots exist exactly when \(\lambda\ge 3\).

- If \(0<\lambda<3\), the quadratic has no real roots, so no such \(x\) exists.
- If \(\lambda=3\), the quadratic becomes
  \[
  x^2-\frac43x+\frac49=0
  \iff
  \left(x-\frac23\right)^2=0,
  \]
  whose only root is \(x=\frac23\). But this is a fixed point: \(f(2/3)=2/3\), so it is excluded.
- If \(3<\lambda\le 4\), the quadratic has two distinct real roots
  \[
  x_{\pm}
  =
  \frac{\lambda+1\pm\sqrt{(\lambda+1)(\lambda-3)}}{2\lambda}.
  \]
  They lie in \((0,1)\): both are positive, and
  \[
  x_+\le 1
  \iff
  \sqrt{(\lambda+1)(\lambda-3)}\le \lambda-1,
  \]
  which holds because
  \[
  (\lambda+1)(\lambda-3)-(\lambda-1)^2=-4<0.
  \]
  Also, for any root of the quadratic,
  \[
  f(x)+x=\frac{\lambda+1}{\lambda},
  \]
  so \(f(x)\) is the other root. Since the two roots are distinct, \(f(x)\ne x\). Thus such an \(x\) exists.

Therefore the required values are exactly
\[

Let \(u=a+bi\) and \(v=c+di\), where \(a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Z\). Thus \(u,v\) are Gaussian integers, i.e. elements of \(\mathbb Z[i]\).

Since
\[
uv=10,
\]
once \(u\) is chosen, \(v\) is forced to be
\[
v=\frac{10}{u}.
\]
So we just need to count the Gaussian integer divisors of \(10\).

In \(\mathbb Z[i]\), use the norm
\[
N(x+iy)=x^2+y^2.
\]
We factor \(10\) in Gaussian integers:

\[
2=-i(1+i)^2,
\]
because \((1+i)^2=2i\), and
\[
5=(2+i)(2-i).
\]
Therefore
\[
10=2\cdot 5=-i(1+i)^2(2+i)(2-i).
\]

The Gaussian primes \(1+i\), \(2+i\), and \(2-i\) are pairwise non-associate, and the units of \(\mathbb Z[i]\) are
\[
\pm 1,\ \pm i.
\]

Since \(\mathbb Z[i]\) is a unique factorization domain, any divisor of \(10\) has the form
\[
u=\varepsilon(1+i)^e(2+i)^f(2-i)^g,
\]
where
\[
\varepsilon\in\{\pm1,\pm i\},\qquad e\in\{0,1,2\},\qquad f,g\in\{0,1\}.
\]

Thus the number of possible Gaussian integer divisors \(u\) is
\[
4\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 2=48.
\]

For each such \(u\), the quotient
\[
v=\frac{10}{u}
\]
is also a Gaussian integer, because the complementary exponents are nonnegative. Hence each divisor \(u\) gives exactly one valid ordered pair \((u,v)\).

Therefore the number of ordered pairs is

\[
\boxed{48}
\]

Let the polynomial be

\[
P(x)=a(x-r_1)(x-r_2)\cdots(x-r_n),
\]

where \(a\in\mathbb Z\) and the \(r_i\) are distinct integers. Since the constant term is \(42\neq 0\), none of the roots is \(0\).

Evaluate at \(x=0\):

\[
42=P(0)=a(-1)^n r_1r_2\cdots r_n.
\]

Thus the integer product \(r_1r_2\cdots r_n\), up to sign, must divide \(42\). Since

\[
42=2\cdot 3\cdot 7,
\]

the product of the absolute values of the roots can contain at most three prime factors counted with multiplicity.

Any integer root with absolute value greater than \(1\) contributes at least one prime factor, so there can be at most \(3\) such roots. The only integer roots with absolute value \(1\) are \(-1\) and \(1\), and since the roots are distinct, there can be at most \(2\) of those.

Therefore the total number of roots is at most

\[
3+2=5.
\]

This bound is attainable. For example,

\[

\]

has integer coefficients, distinct integer roots \(-1,1,2,3,7\), and

\[
P(0)=1\cdot(-1)\cdot(-2)\cdot(-3)\cdot(-7)=42.
\]

Hence the largest possible number of integer roots is

\[
\boxed{5}.

Let the area of rectangle \(ABCD\) be \(K\).

Define two ratios:

\[
x=\frac{BE}{BC}, \qquad y=\frac{CF}{CD}.
\]

Since \(ABCD\) is a rectangle, the three given triangles are right triangles.

### 1. Area of \(\triangle ABE\)

\[
[ABE]=\frac12\cdot AB\cdot BE
=\frac12\cdot K\cdot x.
\]

Given \([ABE]=8\),

\[
\frac12 Kx=8 \implies Kx=16. \tag{1}
\]

### 2. Area of \(\triangle ADF\)

Since \(DF = CD-CF = CD(1-y)\),

\[
[ADF]=\frac12\cdot AD\cdot DF
=\frac12\cdot K\cdot (1-y).
\]

Given \([ADF]=5\),

\[
\frac12 K(1-y)=5 \implies K(1-y)=10. \tag{2}
\]

### 3. Area of \(\triangle CEF\)

Since \(CE=BC-BE=BC(1-x)\) and \(CF=CD\cdot y\),

\[
[CEF]=\frac12\cdot CE\cdot CF
=\frac12 K(1-x)y.
\]

Given \([CEF]=9\),

\[
\frac12 K(1-x)y=9 \implies K(1-x)y=18. \tag{3}
\]

From (1) and (2),

\[
x=\frac{16}{K}, \qquad 1-y=\frac{10}{K} \implies y=1-\frac{10}{K}.
\]

Substitute into (3):

\[
K\left(1-\frac{16}{K}\right)\left(1-\frac{10}{K}\right)=18.
\]

Simplify:

\[
\frac{(K-16)(K-10)}{K}=18.
\]

Thus

\[
(K-16)(K-10)=18K,
\]

\[
K^2-26K+160=18K,
\]

\[
K^2-44K+160=0.
\]

Solving,

\[
K=\frac{44\pm\sqrt{44^2-4\cdot160}}{2}
=\frac{44\pm36}{2}.
\]

So

\[
K=40 \quad \text{or} \quad K=4.
\]

But \(K=4\) is impossible because \(\triangle ABE\) alone has area \(8\), and also \(x=16/K\le 1\) requires \(K\ge 16\).

Therefore, the area of rectangle \(ABCD\) is

\[
\boxed{40}
\]

\[

The radicands are always positive:
\[
x^2-10x+34=(x-5)^2+9>0,\qquad x^2+4>0,
\]
so \(f\) is defined and continuous for all real \(x\).

Interpret the function geometrically. Let
\[
P=(x,0),\qquad A=(5,3),\qquad B=(0,2).
\]
Then
\[
PA=\sqrt{(x-5)^2+3^2}=\sqrt{x^2-10x+34},
\]
\[
PB=\sqrt{x^2+2^2}=\sqrt{x^2+4}.
\]
Thus
\[
f(x)=PA-PB.
\]

### Upper bound
By the triangle inequality in \(\triangle PAB\),
\[
PA\le PB+AB.
\]
Hence
\[
f(x)=PA-PB\le AB.
\]
Now
\[
AB=\sqrt{(5-0)^2+(3-2)^2}=\sqrt{25+1}=\sqrt{26}.
\]
So
\[
f(x)\le \sqrt{26}.
\]

Equality can occur when \(P,B,A\) are collinear with \(B\) between \(P\) and \(A\). The line through \(A=(5,3)\) and \(B=(0,2)\) is
\[
y=2+\frac{x}{5}.
\]
It meets the \(x\)-axis when \(y=0\), giving
\[
0=2+\frac{x}{5}\implies x=-10.
\]
Check:
\[
f(-10)=\sqrt{(-10)^2-10(-10)+34}-\sqrt{(-10)^2+4}
=\sqrt{234}-\sqrt{104}
=3\sqrt{26}-2\sqrt{26}
=\sqrt{26}.
\]
So the maximum value is \(\sqrt{26}\), and it is attained.

### Lower bound
We show that \(f(x)>-5\) for every real \(x\). Write
\[
f(x)+5=\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}+5-\sqrt{x^2+4}.
\]
Rationalize:
\[
f(x)+5
=
\frac{\left(\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}+5\right)^2-(x^2+4)}
{\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}+5+\sqrt{x^2+4}}.
\]
The denominator is positive. The numerator simplifies:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left(\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}+5\right)^2-(x^2+4)\\
&=x^2-10x+34+25+10\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}-x^2-4\\
&=10\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}+55-10x\\
&=10\left(\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}+\frac{11}{2}-x\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
So it remains to prove
\[
\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}+\frac{11}{2}-x>0.
\]

If \(x\le \frac{11}{2}\), then since
\[
x^2-10x+34=(x-5)^2+9\ge 9,
\]
we have
\[
\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}\ge 3,
\]
and therefore
\[
\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}+\frac{11}{2}-x\ge 3+\frac{11}{2}-x>0.
\]

If \(x>\frac{11}{2}\), then
\[
\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}
=\sqrt{(x-5)^2+9}>x-5,
\]
so
\[
\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}+\frac{11}{2}-x
>
(x-5)+\frac{11}{2}-x
=
\frac12>0.
\]

Thus
\[
f(x)+5>0\quad\text{for all }x,
\]
so
\[
f(x)>-5.
\]

Now find the limiting behavior as \(x\to\infty\). Rationalizing,
\[
f(x)=\frac{x^2-10x+34-(x^2+4)}
{\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}+\sqrt{x^2+4}}
=
\frac{30-10x}{\sqrt{x^2-10x+34}+\sqrt{x^2+4}}.
\]
Divide numerator and denominator by \(x\) for \(x>0\):
\[
f(x)=
\frac{-10+\frac{30}{x}}
{\sqrt{1-\frac{10}{x}+\frac{34}{x^2}}+\sqrt{1+\frac{4}{x^2}}}
\longrightarrow
\frac{-10}{1+1}=-5.
\]
So \(-5\) is the infimum, but it is not attained.

Since \(f\) is continuous, for every \(y\) with
\[
-5<y<\sqrt{26},
\]
there exists some \(x\) such that \(f(x)=y\). The value \(\sqrt{26}\) is attained at \(x=-10\).

Therefore, the range is
\[
\boxed{(-5,\sqrt{26}]}
\]

\]

For \(n\ge 3\), expanding along the last row gives the recurrence

\[
D_n=10D_{n-1}-9D_{n-2}.
\]

This is because the diagonal entry contributes \(10D_{n-1}\), and the lower off-diagonal entry contributes \(-3\cdot 3D_{n-2}=-9D_{n-2}\).

The characteristic equation is

\[
r^2-10r+9=0,
\]

so

\[
(r-1)(r-9)=0,
\]

giving \(r=1,9\). Thus

\[
D_n=A9^n+B.
\]

Using \(D_1=10\) and \(D_2=91\),

\[
9A+B=10,
\]
\[
81A+B=91.
\]

Subtracting,

\[
72A=81 \implies A=\frac{9}{8}.
\]

Then

\[
B=10-9\cdot \frac{9}{8}=10-\frac{81}{8}=-\frac{1}{8}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
D_n=\frac{9}{8}9^n-\frac{1}{8}
=\frac{9^{n+1}-1}{8}.
\]

Now compute

\[
8D_n+1
=8\left(\frac{9^{n+1}-1}{8}\right)+1
=9^{n+1}.
\]

So

\[
\frac{1}{8D_n+1}=\frac{1}{9^{n+1}}.
\]

Hence the desired sum is

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{8D_n+1}
=
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{9^{n+1}}
=
\sum_{k=2}^{\infty}\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)^k.

a+b+c+d=1.

Therefore,

\[
ab+bc+cd \le ab+bc+bd
= b(a+c+d).

Using \(a+b+c+d=1\), we get \(a+c+d=1-b\). Hence

\[

Now

Therefore,

= c(a+b+d).

Using \(a+b+c+d=1\), we get \(a+b+d=1-c\). Hence

Again,

We want to find positive real triples \((x,y,z)\) such that

\[
\left(x+\frac1y\right)\left(y+\frac1z\right)\left(z+\frac1x\right)=8.
\]

By the AM-GM inequality,

\[
x+\frac1y \ge 2\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},
\]
\[
y+\frac1z \ge 2\sqrt{\frac{y}{z}},
\]
\[
z+\frac1x \ge 2\sqrt{\frac{z}{x}}.
\]

Multiplying these three inequalities gives

\[
\left(x+\frac1y\right)\left(y+\frac1z\right)\left(z+\frac1x\right)
\ge
\left(2\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}\right)\left(2\sqrt{\frac{y}{z}}\right)\left(2\sqrt{\frac{z}{x}}\right).
\]

The right-hand side simplifies to

\[
8\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}\cdot \frac{y}{z}\cdot \frac{z}{x}}=8.
\]

Thus the product is always at least \(8\). Since the equation says it is exactly \(8\), equality must hold in all three AM-GM inequalities. Therefore,

\[
x=\frac1y,\qquad y=\frac1z,\qquad z=\frac1x.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
xy=1,\qquad yz=1,\qquad zx=1.
\]

From \(xy=1\) and \(yz=1\), we get \(x=z\). Then \(zx=1\) becomes \(x^2=1\), so since \(x>0\), we have \(x=1\). Then \(y=z=1\).

Thus the only positive real solution is

\[
(x,y,z)=(1,1,1).
\]

Therefore, the number of ordered triples is

\[
\boxed{1}
\]

Let

\[
x=\cos\theta.
\]

We are told that \(x\) is irrational, while

\[
\cos 2\theta,\cos 3\theta,\dots,\cos n\theta
\]

are all rational.

First,

\[
\cos 2\theta=2x^2-1
\]

is rational. Therefore

\[
x^2=\frac{\cos 2\theta+1}{2}
\]

is rational.

Now suppose \(n\ge 5\). Then \(\cos 3\theta\) is also rational. Using the triple-angle formula,

\[
\cos 3\theta=4x^3-3x=x(4x^2-3).
\]

Since \(x^2\) is rational, \(4x^2-3\) is rational. If \(4x^2-3\neq 0\), then \(\cos 3\theta\) would be a nonzero rational multiple of the irrational number \(x\), which would be irrational. That is impossible. Hence

\[
4x^2-3=0,
\]

so

\[
x^2=\frac34.
\]

Now check \(\cos 5\theta\). We have

\[
\cos 5\theta=16x^5-20x^3+5x=x(16x^4-20x^2+5).
\]

Substitute \(x^2=\frac34\):

\[
16x^4-20x^2+5
=
16\left(\frac{9}{16}\right)-20\left(\frac34\right)+5
=
9-15+5
=
-1.
\]

Thus

\[
\cos 5\theta=-x,
\]

which is irrational, contradicting the requirement that \(\cos 5\theta\) be rational. Therefore \(n\) cannot be \(5\) or larger.

It remains to show that \(n=4\) is possible. Take

\[
\theta=\frac{\pi}{6}.
\]

Then

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}
\]

is irrational, while

\[
\cos 2\theta=\cos\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac12,
\]

\[
\cos 3\theta=\cos\frac{\pi}{2}=0,
\]

\[
\cos 4\theta=\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}=-\frac12.
\]

These are all rational. Therefore the largest possible value of \(n\) is

\[
\boxed{4}.
\]

We solve the linear recurrence

\[
a_n=\sqrt3\,a_{n-1}-a_{n-2},\qquad a_0=2,\ a_1=1.
\]

The characteristic equation is

\[
r^2-\sqrt3 r+1=0.
\]

Its roots are

\[
r=\frac{\sqrt3\pm i}{2}.
\]

Notice that

\[
\frac{\sqrt3+i}{2}=e^{i\pi/6},\qquad \frac{\sqrt3-i}{2}=e^{-i\pi/6}.
\]

Thus

\[
a_n=A\cos\left(\frac{n\pi}{6}\right)+B\sin\left(\frac{n\pi}{6}\right).
\]

Using \(a_0=2\),

\[
2=A\cos 0+B\sin 0=A,
\]

so \(A=2\).

Using \(a_1=1\),

\[
1=2\cos\frac{\pi}{6}+B\sin\frac{\pi}{6}
=2\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+B\cdot\frac12.
\]

Wait, more directly:

\[
a_n=2\cos\left(\frac{n\pi}{6}\right)+B\sin\left(\frac{n\pi}{6}\right),
\]

and

\[
a_1=2\sin\frac{\pi}{6}+B\cos\frac{\pi}{6}
=2\cdot\frac12+B\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}
=1+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}B.
\]

Since \(a_1=1\), we get \(B=0\). Therefore

\[
a_n=2\cos\left(\frac{n\pi}{6}\right).
\]

So

\[
a_{100}=2\cos\left(\frac{100\pi}{6}\right)
=2\cos\left(\frac{50\pi}{3}\right).
\]

Reduce the angle modulo \(2\pi\):

\[
\frac{50\pi}{3}=16\pi+\frac{2\pi}{3}.
\]

Thus

\[
a_{100}=2\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}=2\left(-\frac12\right)=-1.
\]

\boxed{-1}

\]

Also,

\[
x^6+1=(x^2)^3+1=(x^2+1)(x^4-x^2+1).
\]

Thus

\[
x^{12}-1=(x-1)(x+1)(x^2+x+1)(x^2+1)(x^2-x+1)(x^4-x^2+1).
\]

Now check that none of these can be factored further over the integers:

- \(x-1\) and \(x+1\) are linear, so irreducible.
- The quadratics
  \[
  x^2+x+1,\quad x^2+1,\quad x^2-x+1
  \]
  have discriminants
  \[
  -3,\quad -4,\quad -3,
  \]
  none of which is a square, so they are irreducible over \(\mathbb Z\).
- For \(x^4-x^2+1\), it has no integer linear factor since
  \[
  1^4-1^2+1=1,\qquad (-1)^4-(-1)^2+1=1.

  \]
  If \(a=0\), then the \(x^2\)-coefficient is \(b+d\), which is either \(2\) or \(-2\), not \(-1\).

\[

\]

factors. Therefore,

\boxed{6}

\[

\]

Complete the square by grouping the quadratic terms:

\[
\begin{aligned}
f(x,y,z)
&=2\left(x+y-\frac12\right)^2+2\left(z-y-\frac12\right)^2+y^2-1.
\end{aligned}
\]

To verify, expand the right-hand side:

\[
\begin{aligned}
&2\left(x+y-\frac12\right)^2+2\left(z-y-\frac12\right)^2+y^2-1\\
&=2(x^2+2xy+y^2-x-y+\tfrac14)\\
&\quad+2(z^2-2yz+y^2-z+y+\tfrac14)+y^2-1\\
&=2x^2+4xy+2y^2-2x-2y+\tfrac12\\
&\quad+2z^2-4yz+2y^2-2z+2y+\tfrac12+y^2-1\\
&=2x^2+5y^2+2z^2+4xy-4yz-2z-2x.
\end{aligned}
\]

Since squares are nonnegative,

\[
2\left(x+y-\frac12\right)^2+2\left(z-y-\frac12\right)^2+y^2 \ge 0.
\]

Thus

\[
f(x,y,z)\ge -1.
\]

Equality occurs when

\[
y=0,\qquad x+y=\frac12,\qquad z-y=\frac12,
\]

so

\[
y=0,\qquad x=\frac12,\qquad z=\frac12.
\]

Therefore, the minimum value is

We can separate the expression into independent factors:

\[
\frac{(x^4+1)(y^4+1)(z^4+1)}{xy^2z}
=
\left(\frac{x^4+1}{x}\right)
\left(\frac{y^4+1}{y^2}\right)
\left(\frac{z^4+1}{z}\right).
\]

Simplify each factor:

\[
\frac{x^4+1}{x}=x^3+\frac1x,
\qquad
\frac{y^4+1}{y^2}=y^2+\frac1{y^2},
\qquad
\frac{z^4+1}{z}=z^3+\frac1z.
\]

So the expression becomes

\[
\left(x^3+\frac1x\right)\left(y^2+\frac1{y^2}\right)\left(z^3+\frac1z\right).
\]

Since the three factors depend on separate positive variables, the minimum is the product of their individual minima.

For \(t>0\),

\[
t^3+\frac1t
=
t^3+\frac1{3t}+\frac1{3t}+\frac1{3t}
\ge
4\sqrt[4]{t^3\left(\frac1{3t}\right)^3}
=
\frac{4}{3^{3/4}},
\]

with equality when

\[
t^3=\frac1{3t}
\implies t^4=\frac13
\implies t=3^{-1/4}.
\]

Thus

\[
\min_{x>0}\left(x^3+\frac1x\right)=\frac{4}{3^{3/4}},
\]

and similarly,

\[
\min_{z>0}\left(z^3+\frac1z\right)=\frac{4}{3^{3/4}}.
\]

For the middle factor,

\[
y^2+\frac1{y^2}\ge 2,
\]

with equality at \(y=1\).

Therefore, the minimum value is

\[
\frac{4}{3^{3/4}}\cdot 2\cdot \frac{4}{3^{3/4}}
=
\frac{32}{3^{3/2}}
=
\frac{32}{3\sqrt3}
=
\frac{32\sqrt3}{9}.
\]

This is of the form \(\frac{a\sqrt b}{c}\) with

Since the identity holds for every real \(x\), it is a polynomial identity.  
The left side has degree \(512\), and we are dividing by a degree-\(2\) polynomial, so \(P\) has degree \(510\). Write

\[
P(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{510} a_k x^k.
\]

For \(0\le n\le 512\), the coefficient of \(x^n\) in \((x^2+x+1)P(x)\) is

\[
a_n+a_{n-1}+a_{n-2},
\]

where \(a_k=0\) if \(k<0\) or \(k>510\). Since

\[
(x^2+x+1)P(x)=x^{512}+x^{256}+1,
\]

we have

\[
a_n+a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}=
\begin{cases}
1, & n=0,256,512,\\
0, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

Now compute the coefficients.

For \(n=0,1,2\):

\[
a_0=1,\qquad a_1+a_0=0 \Rightarrow a_1=-1,\qquad a_2+a_1+a_0=0 \Rightarrow a_2=0.
\]

For \(3\le n\le 255\), the recurrence is

\[
a_n=-a_{n-1}-a_{n-2}.
\]

This recurrence has period \(3\), so the pattern

\[
1,-1,0
\]

repeats. Thus for \(0\le n\le 255\),

\[
a_n=
\begin{cases}
1, & n\equiv 0 \pmod 3,\\
-1, & n\equiv 1 \pmod 3,\\
0, & n\equiv 2 \pmod 3.
\end{cases}
\]

At \(n=256\),

\[
a_{256}+a_{255}+a_{254}=1.
\]

Since \(a_{255}=1\) and \(a_{254}=0\), we get

\[
a_{256}=0.
\]

Then for \(257\le n\le 510\), the same zero-coefficient recurrence gives the repeating pattern

\[
0,-1,1.
\]

So for \(256\le n\le 510\),

\[
a_n=
\begin{cases}
0, & n\equiv 1 \pmod 3,\\
-1, & n\equiv 2 \pmod 3,\\
1, & n\equiv 0 \pmod 3.
\end{cases}
\]

In particular, the nonzero coefficients occur at

\[
0,1,3,4,\dots,252,253,255
\]

and

\[
257,258,260,261,\dots,509,510.
\]

The first list has \(85\) pairs plus the extra term \(255\), so it contributes

\[
2\cdot 85+1=171
\]

nonzero coefficients.

The second list has \(85\) pairs, contributing

\[
2\cdot 85=170
\]

nonzero coefficients.

Therefore the total number of nonzero coefficients is

\[
171+170=341.
\]

\[
\boxed{341}

Let \(O\) be the center of the circle, and use \(O\) as the origin. Write the position vectors of the four points as \(\vec A,\vec B,\vec C,\vec D\). Since all four points lie on the same circle,

\[
|\vec A|=|\vec B|=|\vec C|=|\vec D|.
\]

Consider the point \(Q\) whose vector is

\[
\vec Q=\frac{\vec A+\vec B+\vec C+\vec D}{2}.
\]

We will show that every one of the six constructed lines passes through \(Q\).

Take a pair of points \(X,Y\) and the complementary pair \(Z,W\). The line in question passes through the midpoint of \(\overline{XY}\), whose vector is

\[
\frac{\vec X+\vec Y}{2},
\]

and is perpendicular to line \(ZW\). Thus a point \(P\) lies on this line exactly when

\[
\left(\vec P-\frac{\vec X+\vec Y}{2}\right)\cdot(\vec W-\vec Z)=0.
\]

Now plug in \(P=Q\):

\[
\vec Q-\frac{\vec X+\vec Y}{2}
=
\frac{\vec X+\vec Y+\vec Z+\vec W}{2}-\frac{\vec X+\vec Y}{2}
=
\frac{\vec Z+\vec W}{2}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\left(\vec Q-\frac{\vec X+\vec Y}{2}\right)\cdot(\vec W-\vec Z)
=
\frac{\vec Z+\vec W}{2}\cdot(\vec W-\vec Z).
\]

But

\[
(\vec Z+\vec W)\cdot(\vec W-\vec Z)
=
|\vec W|^2-|\vec Z|^2
=0,
\]

because \(Z\) and \(W\) lie on the same circle centered at the origin.

So every one of the six lines passes through \(Q\). Hence the common point \(P\) satisfies

\[
\vec P=\frac12\vec A+\frac12\vec B+\frac12\vec C+\frac12\vec D.
\]

Thus

\[
a=b=c=d=\frac12,
\]

and

\[
a+b+c+d=4\cdot \frac12=2.
\]

\[
\boxed{2}

Then the product becomes

P=\prod_{k=0}^{\infty}\left(1+x^{2^k}\right).

Use the finite identity

\[
(1-x)(1+x)(1+x^2)(1+x^4)\cdots(1+x^{2^n})=1-x^{2^{n+1}}.
\]

This follows repeatedly from

\[
(1-y)(1+y)=1-y^2.

Thus, for the partial product

\[
P_n=\prod_{k=0}^{n}\left(1+x^{2^k}\right),

we have

\[
P_n=\frac{1-x^{2^{n+1}}}{1-x}.
\]

Since \(|x|<1\), we have

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}x^{2^{n+1}}=0.
\]

Therefore,

\[
P=\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n=\frac{1}{1-x}.
\]

Substitute \(x=\frac1{14}\):

\[
P=\frac{1}{1-\frac1{14}}
=\frac{1}{\frac{13}{14}}
=\frac{14}{13}.

Let the center of the regular hexagon be \(O\). This is also the center of the large sphere.

1. **Radius of the large sphere**

   The centers of the six small spheres are at the vertices of a regular hexagon of side length \(2\). A regular hexagon with side length \(2\) has circumradius \(2\), so each small sphere’s center is distance \(2\) from \(O\).

   Each small sphere has radius \(1\) and is internally tangent to the large sphere, so the large sphere has radius

   \[
   R = 2+1 = 3.
   \]

2. **Position of the eighth sphere**

   Let the eighth sphere have radius \(r\), and let its center be \(P\).

   Since the eighth sphere is externally tangent to all six small spheres of radius \(1\), its distance from each small-sphere center is

   \[
   r+1.
   \]

   Thus \(P\) is equidistant from all six vertices of the regular hexagon. By symmetry, \(P\) must lie on the line through \(O\) perpendicular to the plane of the hexagon.

   Let the distance from \(O\) to \(P\) be \(h\). Since the eighth sphere is internally tangent to the large sphere of radius \(3\),

   \[
   h+r=3.
   \]

   So

   \[
   h=3-r.
   \]

3. **Use tangency to the small spheres**

   A small sphere’s center is distance \(2\) from \(O\) in the plane of the hexagon, and \(P\) is height \(h\) above that plane. Therefore the distance from \(P\) to any small sphere’s center is

   \[
   \sqrt{2^2+h^2}.
   \]

   This must equal \(r+1\), so

   \[
   \sqrt{4+h^2}=r+1.
   \]

   Substitute \(h=3-r\):

   \[
   \sqrt{4+(3-r)^2}=r+1.
   \]

   Square both sides:

   \[
   4+(3-r)^2=(r+1)^2.
   \]

   Expand:

   \[
   4+9-6r+r^2=r^2+2r+1.
   \]

   Simplify:

   \[
   13-6r=1+2r
   \]

   \[
   12=8r
   \]

   \[
   r=\frac32.
   \]

Thus the radius of the eighth sphere is

\[
\boxed{\frac32}
\]

Let

\[
S=\frac{a}{b+c}+\frac{b}{c+a}+\frac{c}{a+b}.
\]

Since \(a,b,c\) are sides of a triangle, \(a,b,c>0\) and

\[
a<b+c,\qquad b<c+a,\qquad c<a+b.
\]

## 1. Lower bound

By Cauchy-Schwarz in Engel form,

\[
S=\sum_{\text{cyc}}\frac{a^2}{a(b+c)}
\ge
\frac{(a+b+c)^2}{a(b+c)+b(c+a)+c(a+b)}.
\]

The denominator is

\[
a(b+c)+b(c+a)+c(a+b)=2(ab+bc+ca),
\]

so

\[
S\ge \frac{(a+b+c)^2}{2(ab+bc+ca)}.
\]

Also,

\[
(a+b+c)^2-3(ab+bc+ca)
=\frac12\bigl((a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2\bigr)\ge 0.
\]

Hence

\[
S\ge \frac32.
\]

Equality occurs when \(a=b=c\), for example in an equilateral triangle. So \(\frac32\) is attainable.

## 2. Upper bound

Because \(a,b,c\) are triangle sides, define

\[
x=\frac{b+c-a}{2},\qquad
y=\frac{c+a-b}{2},\qquad
z=\frac{a+b-c}{2}.
\]

Then \(x,y,z>0\), and

\[
a=y+z,\qquad b=z+x,\qquad c=x+y.
\]

Thus

\[
\begin{aligned}
S
&=\frac{y+z}{2x+y+z}
+\frac{z+x}{2y+z+x}
+\frac{x+y}{2z+x+y} \\[2mm]
&=3-2\left(
\frac{x}{2x+y+z}
+\frac{y}{2y+z+x}
+\frac{z}{2z+x+y}
\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

Let

\[
U=\frac{x}{2x+y+z}
+\frac{y}{2y+z+x}
+\frac{z}{2z+x+y}.
\]

Again by Cauchy-Schwarz,

\[
\begin{aligned}
U
&=\sum_{\text{cyc}}\frac{x^2}{x(2x+y+z)} \\
&\ge
\frac{(x+y+z)^2}{\sum_{\text{cyc}}x(2x+y+z)}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Now

\[
\sum_{\text{cyc}}x(2x+y+z)
=
2(x^2+y^2+z^2)+2(xy+yz+zx).
\]

Set

\[
A=x^2+y^2+z^2+xy+yz+zx.
\]

Then

\[
(x+y+z)^2=A+(xy+yz+zx)>A
\]

because \(x,y,z>0\). Therefore

\[
U>\frac{A}{2A}=\frac12.
\]

So

\[
S=3-2U<3-1=2.
\]

Thus every possible value satisfies

\[
\frac32\le S<2.
\]

## 3. Every value in \(\left[\frac32,2\right)\) occurs

Take \(a=b=1\) and \(c=t\), where \(0<t\le 1\). These are valid triangle sides. Then

\[
S(t)=\frac{1}{1+t}+\frac{1}{1+t}+\frac{t}{2}
=\frac{2}{1+t}+\frac{t}{2}.
\]

We have

\[
S(1)=\frac32
\]

and

\[
\lim_{t\to 0^+}S(t)=2.
\]

Also,

\[
S'(t)=\frac12-\frac{2}{(1+t)^2}
=\frac{(t-1)(t+3)}{2(1+t)^2}<0
\]

for \(0<t<1\). Hence \(S(t)\) is continuous and strictly decreasing on \((0,1]\), so it takes every value in

\[
\left[\frac32,2\right).
\]

Therefore the set of all possible values is

\[
\boxed{\left[\frac{3}{2},\,2\right)}.
\]

We need to solve

\[
30x \equiv 42 \pmod{47}.
\]

Since \(\gcd(30,47)=1\), we can multiply by the inverse of \(30\) modulo \(47\).

Find \(30^{-1} \pmod{47}\) using the extended Euclidean algorithm:

\[
47 = 30\cdot 1 + 17
\]
\[
30 = 17\cdot 1 + 13
\]
\[
17 = 13\cdot 1 + 4
\]
\[
13 = 4\cdot 3 + 1
\]

Back-substitute:

\[
1 = 13 - 4\cdot 3
\]
\[
1 = 13 - (17 - 13)\cdot 3 = 4\cdot 13 - 3\cdot 17
\]
\[
1 = 4(30 - 17) - 3\cdot 17 = 4\cdot 30 - 7\cdot 17
\]
\[
1 = 4\cdot 30 - 7(47 - 30) = 11\cdot 30 - 7\cdot 47
\]

Thus,

\[
30 \cdot 11 \equiv 1 \pmod{47},
\]

so \(30^{-1} \equiv 11 \pmod{47}\).

Now multiply both sides of the original congruence by \(11\):

\[
x \equiv 42 \cdot 11 \pmod{47}
\]

\[
x \equiv 462 \pmod{47}.
\]

Since

\[
462 = 47\cdot 9 + 39,
\]

we have

\[
x \equiv 39 \pmod{47}.
\]

The smallest positive integer satisfying the congruence is therefore

\[
\boxed{39}
\]

We want to minimize

\[

\]

subject to

\[
2x+3y=5,\qquad x,y>0.
\]

Rewrite the expression in a form where Cauchy-Schwarz can be applied:

\[
\frac{3}{x}=\frac{6}{2x},\qquad \frac{2}{y}=\frac{6}{3y}.
\]

Thus,

\[
\frac{3}{x}+\frac{2}{y}
=
\frac{(\sqrt6)^2}{2x}+\frac{(\sqrt6)^2}{3y}.
\]

By Cauchy-Schwarz,

\[
\left(\frac{(\sqrt6)^2}{2x}+\frac{(\sqrt6)^2}{3y}\right)(2x+3y)
\ge
(\sqrt6+\sqrt6)^2.
\]

So

\[
\left(\frac{3}{x}+\frac{2}{y}\right)(5)
\ge
(2\sqrt6)^2=24.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\frac{3}{x}+\frac{2}{y}\ge \frac{24}{5}.
\]

Equality occurs when

\[
\frac{\sqrt6}{2x}=\frac{\sqrt6}{3y}
\]

which simplifies to

\[
2x=3y.
\]

Using \(2x+3y=5\), we get

\[
2x+2x=5 \implies 4x=5 \implies x=\frac54,
\]

and then

\[
y=\frac{2x}{3}=\frac{5}{6}.
\]

At this point,

\[
\frac{3}{x}+\frac{2}{y}
=
\frac{3}{5/4}+\frac{2}{5/6}
=
\frac{12}{5}+\frac{12}{5}
=
\frac{24}{5}.
\]

Hence the minimum value is

\[
\boxed{\frac{24}{5}}
\]

f(f(x))=x,\qquad f(x)=|3x-1|.

Since the left side is an absolute value, we must have \(x\ge 0\).

Now split based on whether \(3x-1\) is negative or nonnegative.

**Case 1: \(x\ge \frac13\).**

Then \(f(x)=3x-1\), so

\[
f(f(x))=|3(3x-1)-1|=|9x-4|.
\]

Thus

\[
|9x-4|=x.
\]

If \(9x-4\ge 0\), i.e. \(x\ge \frac49\), then

\[
9x-4=x \implies 8x=4 \implies x=\frac12,
\]

which is valid.

If \(9x-4<0\), i.e. \(x<\frac49\), then

\[
-(9x-4)=x \implies 4-9x=x \implies 10x=4 \implies x=\frac25,
\]

which is valid.

**Case 2: \(0\le x<\frac13\).**

Then \(f(x)=1-3x\), so

\[
f(f(x))=|3(1-3x)-1|=|2-9x|.
\]

Thus

\[
|2-9x|=x.
\]

If \(2-9x\ge 0\), i.e. \(x\le \frac29\), then

\[
2-9x=x \implies 10x=2 \implies x=\frac15,
\]

which is valid.

If \(2-9x<0\), i.e. \(x>\frac29\), then

\[
9x-2=x \implies 8x=2 \implies x=\frac14,
\]

which is valid.

\[
\boxed{\frac15,\frac14,\frac25,\frac12}
\]

Matching coefficients with \(x^8+98x^4+1\), we need

\[

Thus

\[
a^2=c^2=2b,
\]

so \(c=\pm a\).

- If \(c=a\), then

\[
b^2+2-4b=98 \implies b^2-4b-96=0 \implies b=12 \text{ or } b=-8,

which gives no integer \(a\) with \(a^2=2b\).

- If \(c=-a\), then

\]

The valid choice is \(b=8\), giving \(a^2=16\), so \(a=\pm4\) and \(c=\mp4\).

By inclusion-exclusion, the number of orders where the first cookie is C or the last cookie is C, or both, is

Since \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) are both degree \(2\), their least common multiple must divide the cubic \(P(x)\). If \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) had no common factor, then their product would have degree \(4\), which cannot divide a cubic. Thus \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\) must share a linear factor, meaning they have a common root.

They cannot be proportional, since comparing leading coefficients would require \(Q_2=2Q_1\), but then the \(x\)-coefficients give

\[
2(k-29)=2k-43 \implies -58=-43,
\]

impossible. So they share exactly one linear factor.

Let the common root be \(r\). Then

\[
r^2+(k-29)r-k=0
\]

and

\[
2r^2+(2k-43)r+k=0.
\]

Subtract twice the first equation from the second:

\[
\bigl(2r^2+(2k-43)r+k\bigr)-\bigl(2r^2+2(k-29)r-2k\bigr)=0.
\]

This simplifies to

\[
15r+3k=0,
\]

so

\[
r=-\frac{k}{5}.
\]

Substitute this into the first equation:

\[
\left(-\frac{k}{5}\right)^2+(k-29)\left(-\frac{k}{5}\right)-k=0.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{k^2}{25}-\frac{k^2}{5}+\frac{29k}{5}-k=0.
\]

Multiply by \(25\):

\[
k^2-5k^2+145k-25k=0,
\]

\[
-4k^2+120k=0,
\]

\[
-4k(k-30)=0.
\]

So

\[
k=0 \quad \text{or} \quad k=30.
\]

The largest value is therefore

\[
\boxed{30}.
\]

\[

So we need to count second-degree polynomials corresponding to ordered triples \((a,r,s)\in\mathbb Z^3\) with

\[
ars=2010.

First factor:

\[

This is squarefree.

ways for the absolute values.

\[

valid sign choices.

Now identify triples that give the same polynomial. Swapping \(r\) and \(s\) does not change the polynomial. If \(r\neq s\), each polynomial with distinct zeros corresponds to exactly two ordered triples.

Since \(a,b,c\) are the roots of

\[
x^3+ax^2+bx+c=0,
\]

counting multiplicity, we have

\[
x^3+ax^2+bx+c=(x-a)(x-b)(x-c).
\]

Expanding the right side,

\[
(x-a)(x-b)(x-c)=x^3-(a+b+c)x^2+(ab+bc+ca)x-abc.
\]

Comparing coefficients gives

\[
a+b+c=-a,
\]
\[
ab+bc+ca=b,
\]
\[
abc=-c.
\]

Thus

\[
2a+b+c=0 \tag{1}
\]

and

\[
c(ab+1)=0. \tag{2}
\]

---

### Case 1: \(c=0\)

From (1),

\[
2a+b=0 \implies b=-2a.
\]

From \(ab+bc+ca=b\), since \(c=0\),

\[
ab=b.
\]

Substitute \(b=-2a\):

\[
a(-2a)=-2a
\]

\[
-2a^2+2a=0
\]

\[
-2a(a-1)=0.
\]

So \(a=0\) or \(a=1\).

- If \(a=0\), then \(b=0\), giving \((a,b,c)=(0,0,0)\).
- If \(a=1\), then \(b=-2\), giving \((a,b,c)=(1,-2,0)\).

---

### Case 2: \(ab=-1\)

Then \(a\neq 0\) and \(b=-\frac1a\). From (1),

\[
c=-2a-b.
\]

Using \(ab+bc+ca=b\), substitute \(c=-2a-b\):

\[
ab+(-2a-b)(a+b)=b.
\]

Expanding,

\[
ab-2a^2-3ab-b^2=b,
\]

so

\[
2a^2+2ab+b^2+b=0.
\]

Now substitute \(b=-\frac1a\):

\[
2a^2-2+\frac1{a^2}-\frac1a=0.
\]

Multiply by \(a^2\):

\[
2a^4-2a^2-a+1=0.
\]

By the rational root theorem, any rational root must be \(\pm1\) or \(\pm \frac12\). Testing these, only \(a=1\) works.

Then

\[
b=-1,
\]

and

\[
c=-2a-b=-2(1)-(-1)=-1.
\]

So this gives \((a,b,c)=(1,-1,-1)\).

\[

\]

First check the small values \(k<5\).

- If \(k=1\), then \(6n+k=6n+1\), so it is not relatively prime to itself: \(\gcd(6n+1,6n+1)=6n+1>1\).
- If \(k=2\), then \(6n+k=6n+2\), so \(\gcd(6n+2,6n+2)=6n+2>1\).
- If \(k=3\), then \(6n+k=6n+3\), so \(\gcd(6n+3,6n+3)=6n+3>1\).
- If \(k=4\), then \(6n+4\) and \(6n+2\) are both even, so

\[
\gcd(6n+4,6n+2)\ge 2,
\]

so \(k=4\) also fails.

Now test \(k=5\). We need to show that \(6n+5\) is relatively prime to each of \(6n+3\), \(6n+2\), and \(6n+1\).

1. Compare \(6n+5\) and \(6n+3\):

\[
(6n+5)-(6n+3)=2.
\]

Thus any common divisor divides \(2\). But both \(6n+5\) and \(6n+3\) are odd, so they cannot share a factor of \(2\). Hence

\[
\gcd(6n+5,6n+3)=1.
\]

2. Compare \(6n+5\) and \(6n+2\):

\[
(6n+5)-(6n+2)=3.
\]

Thus any common divisor divides \(3\). But

\[
6n+2 \equiv 2 \pmod 3,
\]

so \(6n+2\) is not divisible by \(3\). Hence

\[
\gcd(6n+5,6n+2)=1.
\]

3. Compare \(6n+5\) and \(6n+1\):

\[
(6n+5)-(6n+1)=4.
\]

\[
\gcd(6n+5,6n+1)=1.
\]

Since \(p\) is an integer, \(f(x)\) has real coefficients. Therefore nonreal roots occur in conjugate pairs. Because none of the roots are real, the four roots can be written as

\[
m \pm in,\qquad r \pm is
\]

where \(m,n,r,s\in\mathbb Z\) and \(n,s\neq 0\).

Then

\[
f(x)=(x^2-2mx+m^2+n^2)(x^2-2rx+r^2+s^2).
\]

Let

\[
U=m^2+n^2,\qquad V=r^2+s^2.
\]

Expanding,

\[
(x^2-2mx+U)(x^2-2rx+V)
\]

\[
=x^4-2(m+r)x^3+(U+V+4mr)x^2-2(mV+rU)x+UV.
\]

Comparing with

\[
x^4-6x^3+26x^2+px+65,
\]

we get

\[
m+r=3,
\]
\[
U+V+4mr=26,
\]
\[
UV=65,
\]
\[
p=-2(mV+rU).
\]

Now \(U,V\) are positive integers with product \(65=5\cdot 13\). The possible pairs are

\[
(U,V)=(1,65),(5,13),(13,5),(65,1).
\]

We check these.

---

### Case 1: \((U,V)=(1,65)\)

Since \(U=m^2+n^2=1\) and \(n\neq 0\), we must have \(m=0\). Then \(r=3\), so

\[
V=r^2+s^2=9+s^2=65
\]

which gives \(s^2=56\), impossible.

Similarly, \((U,V)=(65,1)\) is impossible.

---

### Case 2: \((U,V)=(5,13)\)

Then

\[
5+13+4mr=26 \implies 4mr=8 \implies mr=2.
\]

Together with \(m+r=3\), we get

\[
(m,r)=(1,2)\quad\text{or}\quad (2,1).
\]

If \(m=1,r=2\), then

\[
U=1+n^2=5 \implies n^2=4,
\]
\[
V=4+s^2=13 \implies s^2=9.
\]

This works.

If \(m=2,r=1\), then

\[
V=1+s^2=13 \implies s^2=12,
\]

which is impossible.

So the working solution is

\[
(m,r,U,V)=(1,2,5,13).
\]

Then

\[
p=-2(mV+rU)=-2(1\cdot 13+2\cdot 5)=-2(23)=-46.
\]

---

### Case 3: \((U,V)=(13,5)\)

By symmetry, the working solution is

\[
(m,r,U,V)=(2,1,13,5),
\]

giving again

\[
p=-2(2\cdot 5+1\cdot 13)=-46.
\]

Thus the only possible value is

\[
\boxed{-46}.
\]

\[

\[

Complete the square in each bracket:

\[
y^2-y=\left(y-\frac12\right)^2-\frac14.

\left(x-y-\frac12\right)^2+\left(y-\frac12\right)^2-\frac14-\frac14+\frac12

So set

We may choose

\[
\tan\theta_{n+2}
=
\frac{\tan\theta_n+\tan\theta_{n+1}}{1-\tan\theta_n\tan\theta_{n+1}}
=
\tan(\theta_n+\theta_{n+1}),

so

\theta_{n+2}\equiv \theta_n+\theta_{n+1}\pmod{\pi}.
\]

Let \(F_0=0,\ F_1=1\) be the Fibonacci numbers. By induction,

\[
\theta_n\equiv F_{n-2}\theta_1+F_{n-1}\theta_2\pmod{\pi}
\qquad (n\ge 2).
\]

Thus

\[
\theta_{2009}
\equiv
F_{2007}\frac{\pi}{4}+F_{2008}\frac{\pi}{6}
=
\frac{\pi}{12}\left(3F_{2007}+2F_{2008}\right).
\]

Since tangent has period \(\pi\), we only need

\[
3F_{2007}+2F_{2008}\pmod{12}.
\]

Now compute the needed Fibonacci residues modulo \(12\). Modulo \(4\), Fibonacci residues repeat with period \(6\):

\[
0,1,1,2,3,1,\ldots
\]

Modulo \(3\), they repeat with period \(8\):

\[
0,1,1,2,0,2,2,1,\ldots
\]

We have

\[
2007\equiv 3\pmod 6,\qquad 2007\equiv 7\pmod 8,
\]

so

\[
F_{2007}\equiv 2\pmod 4,\qquad F_{2007}\equiv 1\pmod 3.

The unique residue modulo \(12\) satisfying these is \(10\).

Similarly,

\[
2008\equiv 4\pmod 6,\qquad 2008\equiv 0\pmod 8,

so

\[
F_{2008}\equiv 3\pmod 4,\qquad F_{2008}\equiv 0\pmod 3,
\]

which gives

\[
F_{2008}\equiv 3\pmod{12}.
\]

Therefore

\[
3F_{2007}+2F_{2008}
\equiv
3(10)+2(3)=36\equiv 0\pmod{12}.
\]

Hence

\[
\theta_{2009}\equiv 0\pmod{\pi},
\]

and so

\[
a_{2009}=\tan\theta_{2009}=\tan 0=0.

\[

\]

The desired expression is symmetric in \(x,y,z\), so relabeling is harmless. Since tangent has period \(\pi\), the three tangent values are
\[

The general solution to \(\sin u=\sin v\) is

\[
u=v+2\pi k \quad\text{or}\quad u=\pi-v+2\pi k.

So either

\[
\pi\cos x=\frac{\pi}{2}-\pi\sin x+2\pi k
\]

giving

\[
\cos x+\sin x=\frac12+2k,
\]

or

\[
\pi\cos x=\pi-\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\pi\sin x\right)+2\pi k
\]

which simplifies to

\[
\pi\cos x=\frac{\pi}{2}+\pi\sin x+2\pi k,
\]

so

\[
\cos x-\sin x=\frac12+2k.
\]

Now \(\sin x\pm\cos x\in[-\sqrt2,\sqrt2]\). Since

\[
\frac12+2k\in[-\sqrt2,\sqrt2]
\]

only when \(k=0\), we must have either

\[
\sin x+\cos x=\frac12
\]

or

\cos x-\sin x=\frac12.

If \(\sin x+\cos x=\frac12\), squaring gives

\[

\sin 2x=-\frac34.

If \(\cos x-\sin x=\frac12\), squaring gives

\]

Both cases are attainable, so the possible values are

\[
\boxed{-\frac{3}{4},\frac{3}{4}}

The function is

\[
f(x)=\arctan x+\frac12\arcsin x.
\]

Since \(\arcsin x\) is only real-valued for \(x\in[-1,1]\), the domain is

\[
[-1,1].
\]

Now differentiate on \((-1,1)\):

\[
f'(x)=\frac{1}{1+x^2}+\frac12\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}.
\]

For every \(x\in(-1,1)\),

\[
\frac{1}{1+x^2}>0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}>0,
\]

so

\[
f'(x)>0.
\]

Thus \(f\) is strictly increasing on \([-1,1]\). Therefore its minimum and maximum occur at the endpoints.

Compute:

\[
f(-1)=\arctan(-1)+\frac12\arcsin(-1)
=-\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}
=-\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{\pi}{4}
=-\frac{\pi}{2},
\]

and

\[
f(1)=\arctan(1)+\frac12\arcsin(1)
=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac12\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}
=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{4}
=\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]

Hence the range is

\[
\boxed{\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]}.
\]

c=1.

Then compare the \(g^2\) coefficients:

2cp = 12.

Now compare the constant terms:

cp^2+q=9.

Substitute \(c=1\) and \(p=6\):

\]

Thus,

Now use

\[
\sin(a-b)=\sin a\cos b-\cos a\sin b.
\]

Since \(a,b\) are acute, we can write

\[
\sin a=\frac{5t}{\sqrt{1+25t^2}},\qquad \cos a=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+25t^2}},
\]

and

\[
\sin b=\frac{t}{\sqrt{1+t^2}},\qquad \cos b=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+t^2}}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\sin(a-b)
=
\frac{5t}{\sqrt{1+25t^2}}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+t^2}}
-
\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+25t^2}}\cdot \frac{t}{\sqrt{1+t^2}}
\]

\[
=\frac{4t}{\sqrt{(1+25t^2)(1+t^2)}}.
\]

We want to maximize this positive expression. Square it:

\[
\sin^2(a-b)=\frac{16t^2}{(1+25t^2)(1+t^2)}.

Let \(x=t^2>0\). Then

\[
\sin^2(a-b)=\frac{16x}{(1+25x)(1+x)}
=\frac{16x}{25x^2+26x+1}.

\sin^2(a-b)=\frac{16}{25x+26+\frac1x}.

To maximize this, minimize

25x+\frac1x+26.

\]

\]

\sin(a-b)\le \frac23.
\]

\[

\]

We complete squares.

First complete the square in \(x\):
\[
3x^2-4xy-6xz
=3\left(x-\frac{2y+3z}{3}\right)^2-\frac43y^2-4yz-3z^2.
\]
Substituting this into \(F\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
F
&=3\left(x-\frac{2y+3z}{3}\right)^2
+\left(12-\frac43\right)y^2
+(27-3)z^2
+(-12-4)yz
-8y-24z\\
&=3\left(x-\frac{2y+3z}{3}\right)^2
+\frac{32}{3}y^2-16yz+24z^2-8y-24z.
\end{aligned}
\]

Now complete the square in \(y\):
\[
\frac{32}{3}y^2-16yz-8y
=
\frac{32}{3}\left(y-\frac{3z}{4}-\frac38\right)^2
-6z^2-6z-\frac32.
\]
Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
F
&=3\left(x-\frac{2y+3z}{3}\right)^2
+\frac{32}{3}\left(y-\frac{3z}{4}-\frac38\right)^2
+18z^2-30z-\frac32.
\end{aligned}
\]

Finally complete the square in \(z\):
\[
18z^2-30z-\frac32
=
18\left(z-\frac56\right)^2-14.
\]
Therefore
\[
F
=
3\left(x-\frac{2y+3z}{3}\right)^2
+\frac{32}{3}\left(y-\frac{3z}{4}-\frac38\right)^2
+18\left(z-\frac56\right)^2
-14.
\]

Each squared term is nonnegative, so
\[
F\ge -14.
\]

for some \(t>0\). Since

\]

we have

\[

\[
\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{OA}{OC}.

\[

\[

\[
\frac{\sqrt{13}}{t\sqrt{13}}=\frac{\sqrt{29}}{OC}
\]

so

\[
\frac1t=\frac{\sqrt{29}}{OC}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
OC=t\sqrt{29}.
\]

Now

\[

\]

Set this equal to \(29t^2\):

Let all angles be in degrees.

First use the double-angle identity:

\[
8\cos^2 10^\circ = 4(2\cos^2 10^\circ)=4(1+\cos 20^\circ).
\]

So the expression becomes

\[
8\cos^2 10^\circ-\frac1{\sin 10^\circ}
=4+4\cos 20^\circ-\frac1{\sin 10^\circ}.
\]

Now we show that

\[
\frac1{\sin 10^\circ}=2+4\cos 20^\circ.
\]

Indeed,

\[
(2+4\cos 20^\circ)\sin 10^\circ
=2\sin 10^\circ+4\sin 10^\circ\cos 20^\circ.
\]

Using the product-to-sum identity

\[
\sin A\cos B=\frac{\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)}2,
\]

with \(A=10^\circ\) and \(B=20^\circ\),

\[
\sin 10^\circ\cos 20^\circ
=\frac{\sin 30^\circ+\sin(-10^\circ)}2
=\frac{\sin 30^\circ-\sin 10^\circ}{2}.
\]

Thus

\[
(2+4\cos 20^\circ)\sin 10^\circ
=2\sin 10^\circ+2(\sin 30^\circ-\sin 10^\circ)
=2\sin 30^\circ.
\]

Since \(\sin 30^\circ=\frac12\),

\[
(2+4\cos 20^\circ)\sin 10^\circ=1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
2+4\cos 20^\circ=\frac1{\sin 10^\circ}.
\]

Substituting back,

\[
8\cos^2 10^\circ-\frac1{\sin 10^\circ}
=4+4\cos 20^\circ-(2+4\cos 20^\circ)
=2.
\]

\[
\boxed{2}
\]

\[

First note that the fixed points of the map \(c\mapsto c^2-2\) satisfy

\[
c^2-2=c
\]

so

\[
c^2-c-2=0 \implies c=2 \quad \text{or} \quad c=-1.
\]

Now consider cases.

---

### Case 1: Double root

If \(r=s\), then we must have

\[
r^2-2=r.
\]

Thus \(r=2\) or \(r=-1\). This gives

\[
(x-2)^2=0 \implies x^2-4x+4=0,
\]

and

\[
(x+1)^2=0 \implies x^2+2x+1=0.
\]

So there are \(2\) equations here.

---

### Case 2: Distinct roots

Suppose \(r\ne s\).

#### Subcase 2a: Both roots are fixed

Then \(\{r,s\}=\{2,-1\}\). This gives

\[
(x-2)(x+1)=x^2-x-2.
\]

So there is \(1\) equation here.

---

#### Subcase 2b: One root is fixed, the other is not

Let the fixed root be \(m\in\{2,-1\}\), and let the other root be \(n\neq m\). Then

\[
n^2-2=m.
\]

If \(m=2\), then

\[
n^2-2=2 \implies n^2=4 \implies n=-2
\]

since \(n\neq 2\).

If \(m=-1\), then

\[
n^2-2=-1 \implies n^2=1 \implies n=1
\]

since \(n\neq -1\).

These give

\[
(x-2)(x+2)=x^2-4
\]

and

\[
(x-1)(x+1)=x^2-1.
\]

So there are \(2\) equations here.

---

#### Subcase 2c: Neither root is fixed

Then each root must map to the other:

\[
r^2-2=s,\qquad s^2-2=r.
\]

Subtracting,

\[
r^2-s^2=s-r.
\]

Thus

\[
(r-s)(r+s)=- (r-s).
\]

Since \(r\neq s\),

\[
r+s=-1.

Using \(s=-1-r\) in \(r^2-2=s\), we get

\[
r^2-2=-1-r

so

\[
r^2+r-1=0.

Similarly, \(s\) satisfies the same equation. Therefore the roots are the two roots of

\[
x^2+x-1=0,
\]

giving the equation

\[
x^2+x-1=0.
\]

So there is \(1\) equation here.

Because \(0\le d\le c\le b\le a\le 4\), we have

\[

\]

and

\[

Now suppose \(z_0\) is a zero of \(P\) with \(|z_0|=1\). Since

\[
P(1)=4+a+b+c+d\ge 4>0,

\[

Thus, at \(z=z_0\),

\[

\[

\le x_0+x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4=4.
\]

\[

\]

\[

\[

j & \text{condition if }x_j>0\\
\hline
0 & z_0^5=1\\

Since \(a\) and \(b\) are chosen uniformly from \([0,1]\), their joint distribution is uniform over the unit square. Ties at exactly \(.5\) have probability \(0\), so the rounding convention at half-integers does not matter.

Rounding rules:

\[
A=\begin{cases}
0,& a<0.5,\\
1,& a>0.5,
\end{cases}
\qquad
B=\begin{cases}
0,& b<0.5,\\
1,& b>0.5.
\end{cases}
\]

Also,

\[
C=\begin{cases}
0,& a+b<0.5,\\
1,& 0.5<a+b<1.5,\\
2,& a+b>1.5.
\end{cases}
\]

We want

\[
A+B=C.
\]

Divide the unit square into four \(\frac12 \times \frac12\) quadrants.

---

### 1. \(A+B=0\)

This occurs when \(a<0.5\) and \(b<0.5\), the lower-left quadrant.

We need \(C=0\), so

\[
a+b<0.5.
\]

In that quadrant, this is the triangle below the line \(a+b=0.5\), with area

\[
\frac12\left(\frac12\right)^2=\frac18.
\]

---

### 2. \(A+B=2\)

This occurs when \(a>0.5\) and \(b>0.5\), the upper-right quadrant.

We need \(C=2\), so

\[
a+b>1.5.
\]

This is the triangle above the line \(a+b=1.5\), also with area

\[
\frac18.
\]

---

### 3. \(A+B=1\)

This occurs in the two remaining quadrants: exactly one of \(a,b\) is greater than \(0.5\).

In each of those quadrants, \(a+b\) is always between \(0.5\) and \(1.5\), so \(C=1\). Therefore all of those quadrants work.

Each quadrant has area

\[
\frac12\cdot \frac12=\frac14,
\]

so together they contribute

\[
\frac14+\frac14=\frac12.
\]

---

Adding the favorable areas:

\[
\frac18+\frac18+\frac12=\frac34.
\]

Thus the probability is

\[
\boxed{\frac34}
\]

Let  
\[
P(x)=x^{2016}+x^{2015}+\cdots+x+1.
\]
Since \(P\) is monic and its roots are \(x_1,\dots,x_{2016}\),
\[
P(x)=\prod_{i=1}^{2016}(x-x_i).
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{P'(x)}{P(x)}=\sum_{i=1}^{2016}\frac1{x-x_i}.
\]
Differentiating,
\[
\left(\frac{P'(x)}{P(x)}\right)'=-\sum_{i=1}^{2016}\frac1{(x-x_i)^2}.
\]
Therefore the desired sum is
\[
S=\sum_{i=1}^{2016}\frac1{(1-x_i)^2}
=-\left(\frac{P'}{P}\right)'(1).
\]

Now set \(d=2016\). Since
\[
P(x)=1+x+\cdots+x^d,
\]
we have
\[
P(1)=d+1,
\]
\[
P'(1)=1+2+\cdots+d=\frac{d(d+1)}2,
\]
and
\[
P''(1)=\sum_{j=2}^d j(j-1)
=\sum_{j=1}^d(j^2-j)
=\frac{d(d+1)(d-1)}3.
\]

Using the quotient rule,
\[
\left(\frac{P'}{P}\right)'(1)
=\frac{P''(1)}{P(1)}-\left(\frac{P'(1)}{P(1)}\right)^2.
\]
Substitute the values:
\[
\left(\frac{P'}{P}\right)'(1)
=\frac{d(d-1)}3-\left(\frac d2\right)^2
=\frac{d(d-1)}3-\frac{d^2}{4}.
\]
Hence
\[
S=-\left(\frac{d(d-1)}3-\frac{d^2}{4}\right)
=\frac{d^2}{4}-\frac{d(d-1)}3
=\frac{d(4-d)}{12}.
\]

With \(d=2016\),
\[
S=\frac{2016(4-2016)}{12}
=\frac{2016(-2012)}{12}
=-168\cdot 2012
=-338016.
\]

\[
\boxed{-338016}
\]

\[

a_1=-1.

\[

=\operatorname{Re}\left[\left(-\frac12+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}i\right)(-1+i)\right]
=-1\cdot\left(-\frac12\right)-1\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}
=\frac12-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.

=\frac12+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.

We are minimizing

\[
f(x)=\max \{|x+15|,\ |x+12|,\ |x+8|,\ |x-1|,\ |x-3|,\ |x-19|\}.
\]

Notice that

\[
|x+15|=|x-(-15)|,\qquad |x-19|=|x-19|.
\]

So among the six quantities, two of them are the distances from \(x\) to \(-15\) and to \(19\). Therefore,

\[
f(x)\ge \max\{|x+15|,|x-19|\}.
\]

For any real \(x\),

\[
|x+15|+|x-19|\ge |19-(-15)|=34.
\]

Thus the larger of the two numbers \(|x+15|\) and \(|x-19|\) is at least

\[
\frac{34}{2}=17.
\]

So for every \(x\),

\[
f(x)\ge 17.
\]

Now choose \(x\) to be the midpoint of \(-15\) and \(19\):

\[
x=\frac{-15+19}{2}=2.
\]

Then

\[
|x+15|=17,\qquad |x-19|=17,
\]

and the other distances are smaller:

\[
|x+12|=14,\quad |x+8|=10,\quad |x-1|=1,\quad |x-3|=1.
\]

Hence

\[
f(2)=17.
\]

Therefore, the minimum value of \(f(x)\) is

\[
\boxed{17}

\]
for all \(n \ge 0\).

Use the Euclidean algorithm:

\[
\gcd(F_n,F_{n+1})
= \gcd(F_n,F_{n+1}-F_n)
= \gcd(F_n,F_{n-1}).
\]

Repeating this process gives

\[
\gcd(F_n,F_{n+1})
= \gcd(F_{n-1},F_n)
= \gcd(F_{n-2},F_{n-1})
= \cdots
= \gcd(F_2,F_1).

Since \(F_2=1\) and \(F_1=1\),

Also, for \(n=0\), \(\gcd(F_0,F_1)=\gcd(0,1)=1\).

Thus every pair of consecutive Fibonacci numbers has greatest common divisor \(1\). Therefore the greatest possible value is

Therefore

Let  
\[
T=a+b+c+d.
\]
Define
\[
x_1=\frac{T}{a},\quad x_2=\frac{T}{b},\quad x_3=\frac{T}{c},\quad x_4=\frac{T}{d}.
\]
Then each \(x_i>1\), and
\[
\frac1{x_1}+\frac1{x_2}+\frac1{x_3}+\frac1{x_4}=1.
\]

Also,
\[
\frac{b+c+d}{a}=\frac{T-a}{a}=\frac{T}{a}-1=x_1-1,
\]
and similarly for the other three terms. Hence the given expression \(E\) satisfies
\[
E=\sum_{i=1}^4 \left\lfloor x_i-1\right\rfloor
=\sum_{i=1}^4 \left(\lfloor x_i\rfloor-1\right)
=\sum_{i=1}^4 \lfloor x_i\rfloor-4.
\]

Let
\[
n_i=\lfloor x_i\rfloor.
\]
We will prove
\[
\sum_{i=1}^4 n_i\ge 13.
\]

Since \(x_i<n_i+1\), we have
\[
\frac1{x_i}>\frac1{n_i+1}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
1=\sum_{i=1}^4 \frac1{x_i}
>
\sum_{i=1}^4 \frac1{n_i+1}.
\]

By Cauchy-Schwarz,
\[
\left(\sum_{i=1}^4 \frac1{n_i+1}\right)
\left(\sum_{i=1}^4 (n_i+1)\right)\ge 16.
\]
Thus
\[
\sum_{i=1}^4 \frac1{n_i+1}
\ge
\frac{16}{\sum_{i=1}^4(n_i+1)}
=
\frac{16}{\sum n_i+4}.
\]
Combining inequalities,
\[
1>\frac{16}{\sum n_i+4},
\]
so
\[
\sum n_i+4>16.
\]
Hence
\[
\sum n_i\ge 13.
\]
Therefore,
\[
E=\sum n_i-4\ge 13-4=9.
\]

It remains to show that \(9\) is attainable. Take
\[
a=b=c=5,\qquad d=4.
\]
Then
\[
\left\lfloor\frac{b+c+d}{a}\right\rfloor
=
\left\lfloor\frac{14}{5}\right\rfloor=2,
\]
and the same holds for the terms with \(b\) and \(c\). Also,
\[
\left\lfloor\frac{a+b+c}{d}\right\rfloor
=
\left\lfloor\frac{15}{4}\right\rfloor=3.
\]
So the total is
\[
2+2+2+3=9.
\]

Thus the minimum value is

\[
\boxed{9}
\]

Let the common magnitude be

\[
|\mathbf a|=|\mathbf b|=|\mathbf c|=m.
\]

Since any pair is orthogonal,

\[
\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf b=\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf c=\mathbf b\cdot \mathbf c=0.
\]

We want the cosine of the angle between \(\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c\):

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c)}
{|\mathbf a|\,|\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c|}.
\]

First compute the numerator:

\[
\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c)
=\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf a+\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b+\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c
=m^2.
\]

Next compute the magnitude of \(\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c\):

\[
|\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c|^2
=(\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c)\cdot(\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c).
\]

Expanding,

\[
|\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c|^2
=|\mathbf a|^2+|\mathbf b|^2+|\mathbf c|^2
+2(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b+\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c+\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c).
\]

Using the orthogonality,

\[
|\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c|^2=m^2+m^2+m^2=3m^2.
\]

Thus,

\[
|\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c|=m\sqrt3.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\cos\theta=\frac{m^2}{m\cdot m\sqrt3}
=\frac1{\sqrt3}.
\]

So the final answer is

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{\sqrt3}}
\]

First,

Second,

\[
\sin 260^\circ \cos 280^\circ
=\frac12\left(\sin(540^\circ)+\sin(-20^\circ)\right).

Since \(\sin 540^\circ=\sin 180^\circ=0\) and \(\sin(-20^\circ)=-\sin 20^\circ\),

\[

=\frac12\left(0-\sin 20^\circ\right)

The \(\sin 20^\circ\) terms cancel, leaving

\boxed{\frac{\sqrt3}{4}}

Let \(n=2011\), and write

\[
P(x)=c_0+c_1x+\cdots+c_nx^n.
\]

We want the coefficient \(c_1\) of \(x\).

For \(k=0,1,\dots,n-1\),

\[
P(2^{k+1})-P(2^k)=(k+1)-k=1.
\]

Define

\[
D(x)=P(2x)-P(x).
\]

Then

\[
D(2^k)=1 \qquad (k=0,1,\dots,n-1).
\]

So \(D(x)-1\) has roots \(1,2,4,\dots,2^{n-1}\). Since \(P\) has degree \(n\), \(D(x)\) also has degree \(n\), hence

\[
D(x)-1=A\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(x-2^k)
\]

for some constant \(A\).

Evaluate at \(x=0\). Since \(D(0)=P(0)-P(0)=0\),

\[
-1=A\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(-2^k).
\]

Now

\[
\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(-2^k)=(-1)^n2^{0+1+\cdots+(n-1)}
=(-1)^n2^{\frac{n(n-1)}2}.
\]

Thus

\[
A=(-1)^{n+1}2^{-\frac{n(n-1)}2}.
\]

Now compare coefficients of \(x\). Since

\[
D(x)=P(2x)-P(x)=\sum_{k=1}^n c_k(2^k-1)x^k,
\]

the coefficient of \(x\) in \(D(x)\) is exactly \(c_1\).

Let

\[
Q(x)=\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(x-2^k).
\]

The coefficient of \(x\) in \(Q(x)\) is

\[
(-1)^{n-1}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\prod_{k\ne j}2^k.
\]

The product of all roots is

\[
\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}2^k=2^{\frac{n(n-1)}2}.
\]

So the coefficient of \(x\) in \(Q(x)\) is

\[
(-1)^{n-1}2^{\frac{n(n-1)}2}
\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}2^{-j}.
\]

The geometric sum is

\[
\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}2^{-j}=2-2^{1-n}.
\]

Therefore the coefficient of \(x\) in \(D(x)-1\), and hence in \(D(x)\), is

\[
A\cdot (-1)^{n-1}2^{\frac{n(n-1)}2}(2-2^{1-n})
=2-2^{1-n}.
\]

With \(n=2011\),

\[
c_1=2-2^{-2010}=2-\frac1{2^{2010}}.
\]

Thus

\[
a=2,\qquad b=2,\qquad c=2010,
\]

and

\[
a+b+c=2+2+2010=2014.
\]

\[
\boxed{2014}
\]

Let the point on the line be

\[
P(t)=(0,0,1)+t(1,1,0)=(t,t,1).
\]

For a chosen point \(P\), the shortest path from the origin to \(P\) and then to \((1,0,0)\) has length

\[
L(t)=|OP|+|P(1,0,0)|.
\]

Compute the two distances:

\[
|OP|^2=t^2+t^2+1=2t^2+1,
\]

and

\[
|P(1,0,0)|^2=(t-1)^2+t^2+1=2t^2-2t+2.
\]

So

\[
L(t)=\sqrt{2t^2+1}+\sqrt{2t^2-2t+2}.
\]

Differentiate:

\[
L'(t)=\frac{2t}{\sqrt{2t^2+1}}+\frac{2t-1}{\sqrt{2t^2-2t+2}}.
\]

Set \(L'(t)=0\). The minimum must occur for \(0<t<\frac12\), where the two terms have opposite signs. Thus

\[
\frac{2t}{\sqrt{2t^2+1}}=\frac{1-2t}{\sqrt{2t^2-2t+2}}.
\]

Squaring and simplifying,

\[
4t^2(2t^2-2t+2)=(1-2t)^2(2t^2+1),
\]

which reduces to

\[
2t^2+4t-1=0.
\]

Thus

\[
t=\frac{-4+\sqrt{24}}{4}=\frac{\sqrt6-2}{2}.
\]

Now evaluate the squared length. Let \(t=\frac{\sqrt6-2}{2}\). Then

\[
2t^2+1=6-2\sqrt6=2(3-\sqrt6),
\]

and

\[
2t^2-2t+2=9-3\sqrt6=3(3-\sqrt6).
\]

Therefore,

\[
L_{\min}=\sqrt{2(3-\sqrt6)}+\sqrt{3(3-\sqrt6)}
=\sqrt{2(3-\sqrt6)}\left(1+\sqrt{\frac32}\right).
\]

So

\[
d^2=L_{\min}^2
=2(3-\sqrt6)\left(1+\sqrt{\frac32}\right)^2.
\]

Since

\[
\left(1+\sqrt{\frac32}\right)^2=\frac{5+2\sqrt6}{2},
\]

we get

\[
d^2=(3-\sqrt6)(5+2\sqrt6)=3+\sqrt6.
\]

\[
\boxed{3+\sqrt6}
\]

Therefore,

\[

Using the cosine addition formula,

\[
\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\cos\alpha\cos\beta-\sin\alpha\sin\beta,
\]

so

\[
\cos\gamma=-\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\sin\alpha\sin\beta-\cos\alpha\cos\beta.
\]

Now consider the desired expression:

\[
\frac{\cos\alpha\cos\beta}{\cos\gamma}
=
\frac{\cos\alpha\cos\beta}{\sin\alpha\sin\beta-\cos\alpha\cos\beta}.

Factor \(\cos\alpha\cos\beta\) from the denominator:

\[
\sin\alpha\sin\beta-\cos\alpha\cos\beta
=
\cos\alpha\cos\beta\left(\tan\alpha\tan\beta-1\right).
\]

Thus,

\[
\frac{\cos\alpha\cos\beta}{\cos\gamma}
=
\frac{1}{\tan\alpha\tan\beta-1}.
\]

We are given

\[
\tan\alpha\tan\beta=\csc\frac{\pi}{3}.

Since

\[

we have

\[

\]
且上底面是下底面沿侧棱方向平移得到的，因此对应边平行，例如  
\[

\]
所以四个侧面本来就是平行四边形。于是，一个四棱柱是否为平行六面体，关键只在于它的底面四边形是否为平行四边形。

反之，若该四棱柱是平行六面体，则它的底面必为平行四边形。

因此，“底面是平行四边形”是一个充要条件。

---

\]

所以第一部分贡献为：

\[
8

-28

\[

\]

因此，\(x^2y^7\) 的系数为

\[

**第一步：求两次都抽到 \(A\) 的概率**

第一次抽到 \(A\) 的概率为

\[
\frac{4}{52}
\]

第一次抽走一张 \(A\) 后，剩下 \(51\) 张牌，其中 \(A\) 还剩 \(3\) 张，所以第二次抽到 \(A\) 的概率为

\[
\frac{3}{51}
\]

因此两次都抽到 \(A\) 的概率为

\[
\frac{4}{52}\times \frac{3}{51}
=
\frac{12}{2652}
=
\frac{1}{221}
\]

---

所以第二次抽到 \(A\) 的概率为

\[
\frac{3}{51}
=
\frac{1}{17}
\]

因此答案为

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{221},\ \frac{1}{17}}
\]

将函数化简：

\[
f(x)=\sin^2 x+\sqrt3\cos x-\frac34
\]

利用恒等式 \(\sin^2 x=1-\cos^2 x\)，得

\[
f(x)=1-\cos^2 x+\sqrt3\cos x-\frac34
\]

整理：

\[
f(x)=-\cos^2 x+\sqrt3\cos x+\frac14
\]

令

\[
t=\cos x
\]

因为 \(x\in\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)，所以

\[
t\in[0,1]
\]

于是问题转化为求二次函数

\[
g(t)=-t^2+\sqrt3 t+\frac14,\quad t\in[0,1]
\]

的最大值。

由于二次项系数为负，抛物线开口向下，最大值在顶点处取得。顶点横坐标为

\[
t=\frac{-\sqrt3}{2(-1)}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}
\]

并且

\[
\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\in[0,1]
\]

所以最大值存在，代入：

\[
g\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)
=-\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2
+\sqrt3\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}
+\frac14
\]

计算：

\[
=-\frac34+\frac32+\frac14
\]

通分：

\[
=-\frac34+\frac64+\frac14=\frac44=1
\]

因此函数最大值为

\[
\boxed{1}
\]

由题意，函数

\[
f(x)=\cos(\omega x+\varphi)\quad(\omega>0,\;0<\varphi<\pi)
\]

的最小正周期为

\[
T=\frac{2\pi}{\omega}.
\]

因为

\[
f(T)=\frac{\sqrt3}{2},
\]

所以

\[
\cos(\omega T+\varphi)=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]

代入 \(T=\frac{2\pi}{\omega}\)，得

\[
\cos(2\pi+\varphi)=\cos\varphi=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]

又因为 \(0<\varphi<\pi\)，所以

\[
\varphi=\frac{\pi}{6}.
\]

已知 \(x=\frac{\pi}{9}\) 是 \(f(x)\) 的零点，因此

\[
f\left(\frac{\pi}{9}\right)=0.
\]

即

\[
\cos\left(\omega\cdot\frac{\pi}{9}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=0.
\]

于是

\[
\omega\cdot\frac{\pi}{9}+\frac{\pi}{6}
=
\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi,\qquad k\in\mathbb Z.
\]

化简得

\[
\omega\cdot\frac{\pi}{9}
=
\frac{\pi}{3}+k\pi,
\]

两边同除以 \(\frac{\pi}{9}\)，得到

\[
\omega=3+9k,\qquad k\in\mathbb Z.
\]

由于 \(\omega>0\)，要使 \(\omega\) 最小，取 \(k=0\)，于是

\omega_{\min}=3.
\]

因此最终答案为

\[
\boxed{3}
\]

令  
\[
b=\ln a\quad (a>0,\ a\ne1\Rightarrow b\ne0).
\]

函数为  
\[
f(x)=2a^x-ex^2.
\]

---

### 1. 求极值点满足的方程

\[
f'(x)=2(a^x\ln a-ex)=2(a^x b-ex).
\]

极值点满足

\[
f'(x)=0
\]

即

\[
ba^x=ex.
\]

因为 \(a^x>0\)，所以 \(b x>0\)。令

\[
t=bx>0.
\]

又因为 \(x=t/b\)，代入 \(ba^x=ex\)：

\[
b e^t=e\frac{t}{b},
\]

整理得

\[
t e^{-t}=\frac{b^2}{e}.
\]

---

### 2. 保证有两个极值点

考虑函数

\[
g(t)=t e^{-t},\qquad t>0.
\]

其导数为

\[
g'(t)=e^{-t}(1-t).
\]

所以 \(g(t)\) 在 \(t=1\) 处取得最大值

\[
g(1)=\frac1e.
\]

要使方程

\[
t e^{-t}=\frac{b^2}{e}
\]

有两个不同正根，需要

\[
0<\frac{b^2}{e}<\frac1e,
\]

即

\[
b^2<1.
\]

因此

\[
-1<b<1,\quad b\ne0.
\]

对应

\[
a\in\left(\frac1e,1\right)\cup(1,e).
\]

设两个根为

\[
0<t_1<1<t_2.
\]

---

### 3. 判断极大值点与极小值点

求二阶导数：

\[
f''(x)=2(a^x b^2-e).
\]

在极值点处满足 \(ba^x=ex\)，于是

\[
b^2a^x=b(ba^x)=bex=e bx=e t.
\]

所以

\[
f''(x)=2(e t-e)=2e(t-1).
\]

因此：

- 当 \(t<1\) 时，\(f''(x)<0\)，对应极大值点；
- 当 \(t>1\) 时，\(f''(x)>0\)，对应极小值点。

所以：

\[
\text{极大值点 } x_{\max}=\frac{t_1}{b},
\]

\[
\text{极小值点 } x_{\min}=\frac{t_2}{b}.
\]

题中已知 \(x_1\) 是极小值点，\(x_2\) 是极大值点，且

\[
x_1<x_2.
\]

即

\[
\frac{t_2}{b}<\frac{t_1}{b}.
\]

由于 \(t_2>t_1>0\)，上式成立当且仅当

\[
b<0.
\]

也就是

\[
\ln a<0.
\]

所以

\[
0<a<1.
\]

结合前面存在两个极值点的条件

\[
a\in\left(\frac1e,1\right)\cup(1,e),
\]

取交集得

\[
a\in\left(\frac1e,1\right).
\]

因此答案为

\[
\boxed{\left(\frac1e,1\right)}
\]

设正方形顶点按顺序为 \(A,B,C,D\)。取

\[
\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf a,\qquad \overrightarrow{AD}=\mathbf b
\]

则因为 \(ABCD\) 是边长为 \(2\) 的正方形，有

\[
|\mathbf a|=|\mathbf b|=2,\qquad \mathbf a\cdot \mathbf b=0.
\]

以 \(A\) 为起点，则

\[
\overrightarrow{AC}=\mathbf a+\mathbf b.
\]

点 \(E\) 是 \(CD\) 的中点，所以

\[
\overrightarrow{AE}
=\frac{1}{2}\left(\overrightarrow{AC}+\overrightarrow{AD}\right)
=\frac{1}{2}\left((\mathbf a+\mathbf b)+\mathbf b\right)
=\frac{1}{2}\mathbf a+\mathbf b.
\]

又

\[
\overrightarrow{BD}
=\overrightarrow{AD}-\overrightarrow{AB}
=\mathbf b-\mathbf a.
\]

因此

\[
\overrightarrow{AE}\cdot \overrightarrow{BD}
=\left(\frac{1}{2}\mathbf a+\mathbf b\right)\cdot(\mathbf b-\mathbf a).
\]

展开：

\[
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{AE}\cdot \overrightarrow{BD}
&=\frac{1}{2}\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf b-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf a
+\mathbf b\cdot \mathbf b-\mathbf b\cdot \mathbf a \\
&=0-\frac{1}{2}\times 2^2+2^2-0 \\
&=-2+4 \\
&=2.
\end{aligned}
\]

所以最终答案为

\[
\boxed{2}
\]

设
\[
f(a,b)=\frac1a+\frac{a}{b^2}+b,\qquad a>0,\ b>0.
\]

**第一步：固定 \(b\)，先对 \(a\) 求最小值。**

由均值不等式，
\[
\frac1a+\frac{a}{b^2}\ge 2\sqrt{\frac1a\cdot \frac{a}{b^2}}
=2\sqrt{\frac1{b^2}}
=\frac2b.
\]

等号成立当且仅当
\[
\frac1a=\frac{a}{b^2}.
\]
因为 \(a,b>0\)，所以
\[
a^2=b^2 \implies a=b.
\]

因此
\[
f(a,b)\ge \frac2b+b.
\]

**第二步：对 \(b\) 求最小值。**

再由均值不等式，
\[
\frac2b+b\ge 2\sqrt{\frac2b\cdot b}=2\sqrt2.
\]

等号成立当且仅当
\[
\frac2b=b.
\]
所以
\[
b^2=2 \implies b=\sqrt2.
\]

结合第一步的等号条件 \(a=b\)，得
\[
a=\sqrt2,\qquad b=\sqrt2.
\]

此时
\[
f(\sqrt2,\sqrt2)
=\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac{\sqrt2}{2}+\sqrt2
=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}+\frac{\sqrt2}{2}+\sqrt2
=2\sqrt2.
\]

因此最小值为

\[
\boxed{2\sqrt2}
\]

设每次活动中：

- 甲猜对的概率为 \(P(A)=\dfrac{5}{6}\)；
- 乙猜对的概率为 \(P(B)=\dfrac{1}{5}\)；
- 甲、乙猜对与否相互独立。

---

### 1. 一次活动中，甲获胜的概率

甲获胜的条件是：**甲猜对，且乙猜错**。

因此

\[
P(\text{甲获胜})
= P(A)P(B^c)
= \frac{5}{6}\left(1-\frac{1}{5}\right)
= \frac{5}{6}\cdot \frac{4}{5}
= \frac{2}{3}.
\]

---

### 2. 3 次活动中，甲至少获胜 2 次的概率

设 3 次活动中甲获胜的次数为 \(X\)。

由于各次活动相互独立，且每次甲获胜的概率为 \(\dfrac{2}{3}\)，所以

\[
X \sim B\left(3,\frac{2}{3}\right).
\]

要求

\[
P(X\ge 2)=P(X=2)+P(X=3).
\]

计算：

\[
P(X=2)=\binom{3}{2}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)
=3\cdot \frac{4}{9}\cdot \frac{1}{3}
=\frac{12}{27},
\]

\[
P(X=3)=\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3
=\frac{8}{27}.
\]

因此

\[
P(X\ge 2)=\frac{12}{27}+\frac{8}{27}
=\frac{20}{27}.
\]

---

最终答案为：

\[
\boxed{\frac{2}{3},\ \frac{20}{27}}
\]

设

\[
f(x)=x\ln\left(x+\sqrt{a+x^2}\right)
\]

要使 \(f(x)\) 为实值偶函数，首先定义域必须关于原点对称。

---

### 1. 分析定义域

要求

\[
a+x^2\ge 0,\qquad x+\sqrt{a+x^2}>0.
\]

- 若 \(a<0\)，设 \(a=-c^2\ (c>0)\)，则要求 \(|x|\ge c\)。  
  当 \(x\le -c\) 时，

  \[
  x+\sqrt{x^2-c^2}\le -c<0,
  \]

  对数无意义，因此定义域只有 \([c,+\infty)\)，不对称，不可能为偶函数。

- 若 \(a=0\)，则

  \[
  x+\sqrt{x^2}=x+|x|,
  \]

  只有 \(x>0\) 时为正，定义域为 \((0,+\infty)\)，也不对称。

因此必须有

\[
a>0.
\]

此时 \(\sqrt{a+x^2}>|x|\)，所以 \(x+\sqrt{a+x^2}>0\)，定义域为全体实数，关于原点对称。

---

### 2. 利用偶函数条件

因为 \(f(x)\) 为偶函数，所以对任意 \(x\in\mathbb R\)，有

\[
f(-x)=f(x).
\]

计算 \(f(-x)\)：

\[
f(-x)=-x\ln\left(-x+\sqrt{a+x^2}\right).
\]

注意到

\[
\left(\sqrt{a+x^2}-x\right)\left(\sqrt{a+x^2}+x\right)=a,
\]

所以

\[
-x+\sqrt{a+x^2}
=\frac{a}{x+\sqrt{a+x^2}}.
\]

于是

\[
\ln\left(-x+\sqrt{a+x^2}\right)
=\ln a-\ln\left(x+\sqrt{a+x^2}\right).
\]

代入得

\[
\begin{aligned}
f(-x)
&=-x\left[\ln a-\ln\left(x+\sqrt{a+x^2}\right)\right] \\
&=x\ln\left(x+\sqrt{a+x^2}\right)-x\ln a \\
&=f(x)-x\ln a.
\end{aligned}
\]

若 \(f(x)\) 为偶函数，则

\[
f(-x)=f(x),
\]

因此

\[

### 1. 先求首项并判断单调性

当 \(n=1\) 时，\(S_1=a_1\)，所以

当 \(n\ge 2\) 时，因为各项均为正数，所以

\]
又由 \(a_nS_n=9\) 得

\]
因此

a_n=\frac{9}{S_n}<\frac{9}{S_{n-1}}=a_{n-1}.
\]
所以 \(\{a_n\}\) 是严格递减数列。

### 2. 判断是否为等比数列

假设 \(\{a_n\}\) 为等比数列，设公比为 \(q\)。因为各项均为正数，所以 \(q>0\)。又 \(a_1=3\)，故
\[
a_2=3q,\qquad a_3=3q^2.
\]

由 \(a_2S_2=9\)，得
\[
3q(3+3q)=9,
\]
即
\[
q(1+q)=1,
\]
所以
\[
q^2+q=1. \tag{1}
\]

由 \(a_3S_3=9\)，得
\[
3q^2(3+3q+3q^2)=9,

即

由 (1) 知

\]
代入 (2) 得
\[
2q^2=1,
\]
即
\[
q^2=\frac12.
\]
但这与 (1) \(q^2+q=1\) 矛盾。

因此 \(\{a_n\}\) 不是等比数列，结论②错误。

函数 \(f(x)\) 的分界点是 \(x=0\)，而 \(f\!\left(x-\frac12\right)\) 的分界点满足

\[
x-\frac12=0 \implies x=\frac12.
\]

因此分三段讨论。

---

### 1. 当 \(x\le 0\) 时

此时 \(x\le 0\)，且

\[
x-\frac12\le -\frac12<0.
\]

所以

\[
f(x)=x+1,\qquad f\left(x-\frac12\right)=x-\frac12+1=x+\frac12.
\]

不等式变为

\[
(x+1)+\left(x+\frac12\right)>1,
\]

即

\[
2x+\frac32>1.
\]

解得

\[
2x>-\frac12,
\]

\[
x>-\frac14.
\]

结合本段条件 \(x\le 0\)，得到

\[
-\frac14<x\le 0.
\]

---

### 2. 当 \(0<x\le \frac12\) 时

此时 \(x>0\)，而

\[
x-\frac12\le 0.
\]

所以

\[
f(x)=2^x,\qquad f\left(x-\frac12\right)=x-\frac12+1=x+\frac12.
\]

不等式为

\[
2^x+x+\frac12>1.
\]

因为 \(x>0\)，所以

\[
2^x>1,
\]

且

\[
x+\frac12>\frac12.
\]

因此

\[
2^x+x+\frac12>1+\frac12=\frac32>1.
\]

所以本段全部满足：

\[
0<x\le \frac12.
\]

---

### 3. 当 \(x>\frac12\) 时

此时

\[
x>0,\qquad x-\frac12>0.
\]

所以

\[
f(x)=2^x,\qquad f\left(x-\frac12\right)=2^{x-\frac12}.
\]

因为 \(x>\frac12\)，所以

\[
2^x>1,\qquad 2^{x-\frac12}>1.
\]

因此

\[
f(x)+f\left(x-\frac12\right)>2>1.
\]

本段全部满足：

\[
x>\frac12.
\]

---

\left(-\frac14,0\right]\cup \left(0,\frac12\right]\cup \left(\frac12,+\infty\right)

\]

### 1. 当 \(0<x\le \frac12\) 时

\[
|2x-1|=1-2x
\]

所以

\[
f(x)=1-2x-2\ln x
\]

求导：

\[
f'(x)=-2-\frac{2}{x}
\]

因为 \(x>0\)，所以

\[
f'(x)<0
\]

因此 \(f(x)\) 在 \(\left(0,\frac12\right]\) 上单调递减。

于是该区间上的最小值在 \(x=\frac12\) 处取得：

\[
f\left(\frac12\right)=1-2\cdot \frac12-2\ln\frac12
=0+2\ln 2
=2\ln 2
\]

---

### 2. 当 \(x\ge \frac12\) 时

\[
|2x-1|=2x-1
\]

所以

\[
f(x)=2x-1-2\ln x
\]

求导：

\[
f'(x)=2-\frac{2}{x}=2\left(1-\frac{1}{x}\right)
\]

令

\[
f'(x)=0
\]

得

\[
x=1
\]

当 \(\frac12<x<1\) 时，\(f'(x)<0\)，函数递减；  
当 \(x>1\) 时，\(f'(x)>0\)，函数递增。

因此 \(x=1\) 是该段区间上的最小值点。

\[
f(1)=|2\cdot 1-1|-2\ln 1=1-0=1
\]

### 3. 比较两段最小值

\boxed{1}

原纸面积为

\[
20\times 12=240\ \text{dm}^2.
\]

每次沿对称轴对折，都是把当前矩形的一条边减半。

设对折 \(k\) 次时，原来 \(20\ \text{dm}\) 这一方向被折了 \(i\) 次，则原来 \(12\ \text{dm}\) 这一方向被折了 \(k-i\) 次，其中

\[
i=0,1,2,\dots,k.
\]

因此对折 \(k\) 次后可能得到的规格为

\[
\frac{20}{2^i}\times \frac{12}{2^{k-i}}.
\]

不同的 \(i\) 给出的规格不会相同，所以共有

\[
k+1
\]

种不同规格。

因此对折 \(4\) 次时，种数为

\[
4+1=5.
\]

---

对折 \(k\) 次后，每种规格的面积都是原面积的 \(\dfrac1{2^k}\)，即

\[
\frac{240}{2^k}.
\]

又有 \(k+1\) 种规格，所以

\[
S_k=(k+1)\cdot \frac{240}{2^k}.
\]

于是

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{n}S_k
=240\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{k+1}{2^k}.
\]

分别求和：

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac1{2^k}=1-\frac1{2^n},
\]

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{k}{2^k}=2-\frac{n+2}{2^n}.
\]

所以

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{k+1}{2^k}
=
\left(2-\frac{n+2}{2^n}\right)+\left(1-\frac1{2^n}\right)
=
3-\frac{n+3}{2^n}.
\]

因此

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{n}S_k
=
240\left(3-\frac{n+3}{2^n}\right)\ \text{dm}^2.
\]

最终答案为

\[
\boxed{5;\ 240\left(3-\dfrac{n+3}{2^n}\right)\ \text{dm}^2}
\]

\[

### 当 \(x\le 1\) 时

\[
f(x)=-x^2+2
\]

要求：

\[
1\le -x^2+2\le 3
\]

先看不等式左边：

\[
1\le -x^2+2
\]

\[
-x^2\ge -1
\]

\[
x^2\le 1
\]

\[
-1\le x\le 1
\]

结合 \(x\le 1\)，得到：

\[
-1\le x\le 1
\]

再看右边：

-x^2+2\le 3
\]

\[
-x^2\le 1
\]

\[
[-1,1]

\]

\[
1\le x+\frac1x-1\le 3

\[
1\le x+\frac1x-1
\]

\[
x+\frac1x\ge 2
\]

\[
y=\pm \frac{x}{\sqrt2}

y=\frac{x}{\sqrt2}

x-\sqrt2 y=0

d=\frac{|3-\sqrt2\cdot 0|}{\sqrt{1^2+(-\sqrt2)^2}}

\boxed{(3,0),\ \sqrt3}
\]

对任意实数 \(x\)，都有

\[
-1\le \sin(x+\varphi)\le 1,\qquad -1\le \cos x\le 1.
\]

因此

\[
f(x)=\sin(x+\varphi)+\cos x\le 1+1=2.
\]

题目给出 \(f(x)\) 的最大值为 \(2\)，说明存在某个 \(x_0\)，使得

\[
f(x_0)=2.
\]

由于两项分别都不超过 \(1\)，它们的和要等于 \(2\)，必须同时取到最大值：

\[
\sin(x_0+\varphi)=1,\qquad \cos x_0=1.
\]

由 \(\cos x_0=1\)，得

\[
x_0=2k\pi,\qquad k\in\mathbb Z.
\]

代入 \(\sin(x_0+\varphi)=1\)，得

\[
\sin(2k\pi+\varphi)=\sin\varphi=1.
\]

因此

\[
\varphi=\frac{\pi}{2}+2n\pi,\qquad n\in\mathbb Z.
\]

所以一个可能的取值为

\[
\boxed{\frac{\pi}{2}}
\]

已知  
\[
\vec a=(1,2),\quad \vec b=(2,-2),\quad \vec c=(1,\lambda)
\]

\[
2\vec a=2(1,2)=(2,4)
\]

\[
2\vec a+\vec b=(2,4)+(2,-2)=(4,2)
\]

因为 \(\vec c\parallel(2\vec a+\vec b)\)，所以两向量对应分量成比例：

\[
\frac{1}{4}=\frac{\lambda}{2}
\]

解得：

\[
\lambda=\frac{1}{2}
\]

因此最终答案为：

\[
\boxed{\frac12}
\]

3x+\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi,\qquad k\in\mathbb Z.

抛物线 \(C:y^2=4x\) 是标准形式 \(y^2=4ax\)，其中

\[
4a=4 \Rightarrow a=1
\]

所以焦点为

\[
F(1,0)
\]

设过焦点且斜率为 \(k\) 的直线为

\[
y=k(x-1)
\]

将其与抛物线 \(y^2=4x\) 联立。由 \(x=\dfrac{y^2}{4}\)，代入直线方程：

\[
y=k\left(\frac{y^2}{4}-1\right)
\]

整理得

\[
ky^2-4y-4k=0
\]

设 \(A(x_1,y_1),B(x_2,y_2)\)，则 \(y_1,y_2\) 是上式方程的两根，因此

\[
y_1+y_2=\frac{4}{k},\qquad y_1y_2=-4
\]

又因为

\[
x_1=\frac{y_1^2}{4},\qquad x_2=\frac{y_2^2}{4}
\]

所以

\[
x_1x_2=\frac{(y_1y_2)^2}{16}=\frac{16}{16}=1
\]

并且

\[
x_1+x_2=\frac{y_1^2+y_2^2}{4}
=\frac{(y_1+y_2)^2-2y_1y_2}{4}
\]

代入根与系数关系：

\[
x_1+x_2=\frac{\left(\frac{4}{k}\right)^2-2(-4)}{4}
=\frac{\frac{16}{k^2}+8}{4}
=\frac{4}{k^2}+2
\]

已知 \(\angle AMB=90^\circ\)，即

\[
\overrightarrow{MA}\cdot \overrightarrow{MB}=0
\]

而

\[
\overrightarrow{MA}=(x_1+1,y_1-1),\qquad
\overrightarrow{MB}=(x_2+1,y_2-1)
\]

因此

\[
(x_1+1)(x_2+1)+(y_1-1)(y_2-1)=0
\]

展开：

\[
x_1x_2+x_1+x_2+1+y_1y_2-(y_1+y_2)+1=0
\]

代入前面的关系：

\[
1+\left(\frac{4}{k^2}+2\right)+1+(-4)-\frac{4}{k}+1=0
\]

化简：

\[
\frac{4}{k^2}-\frac{4}{k}+1=0
\]

两边乘以 \(k^2\)：

\[
4-4k+k^2=0
\]

即

\[
(k-2)^2=0
\]

所以

\[
k=2
\]

因此最终答案为

\[
\boxed{2}
\]

设公共项为 \(x\)。

数列 \(\{2n-1\}\) 的项为奇数：
\[
1,3,5,7,9,11,\dots
\]

数列 \(\{3n-2\}\) 的项为：
\[
1,4,7,10,13,\dots
\]
即满足
\[
x\equiv 1 \pmod 3
\]

公共项既要为奇数，又要满足 \(x\equiv 1\pmod 3\)，因此
\[
x\equiv 1 \pmod 6
\]

所以公共项从小到大排列为
\[
1,7,13,19,\dots
\]

即
\[
a_n=6n-5
\]

前 \(n\) 项和为
\[
S_n=\frac{n\left[a_1+a_n\right]}{2}
=\frac{n\left[1+(6n-5)\right]}{2}
\]

\[
S_n=\frac{n(6n-4)}{2}
=3n^2-2n
\]

因此答案是

\[
\boxed{3n^2-2n}
\]

由向量模长公式：

\[
|\vec a+\vec b|^2=(\vec a+\vec b)\cdot(\vec a+\vec b)
\]

展开得：

\[
|\vec a+\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2+2\vec a\cdot \vec b+|\vec b|^2
\]

题目给出：

\[
|\vec a+\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2
\]

因此：

\[
|\vec a|^2+2\vec a\cdot \vec b+|\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2
\]

化简得：

\[
2\vec a\cdot \vec b=0
\]

所以：

\[
\vec a\cdot \vec b=0
\]

已知：

\[
\vec a=(m,1),\qquad \vec b=(1,2)
\]

则点积为：

\[
\vec a\cdot \vec b=m\cdot 1+1\cdot 2=m+2
\]

由 \(\vec a\cdot \vec b=0\)，得：

\[
m+2=0
\]

解得：

\[
m=-2
\]

因此最终答案为：

\[
\boxed{-2}
\]

设等比数列 \(\{a_n\}\) 的首项为 \(a\)，公比为 \(q\)，则

\[
a_1=a,\qquad a_2=aq,\qquad a_3=aq^2,\qquad a_4=aq^3.
\]

由题意

\[
a_1+a_3=10,\qquad a_2+a_4=5.
\]

因为

\[
a_2+a_4=aq+aq^3=q(a+a q^2)=q(a_1+a_3),
\]

所以

\[
5=q\cdot 10,
\]

从而

\[
q=\frac12.
\]

代入 \(a_1+a_3=10\)，得

\[
a(1+q^2)=10,
\]

即

\[
a\left(1+\frac14\right)=10,
\]

\[
a\cdot \frac54=10,
\]

所以

\[
a=8.
\]

因此

\[
a_n=8\left(\frac12\right)^{n-1}.
\]

前 \(n\) 项乘积为

\[
P_n=a_1a_2\cdots a_n
=\prod_{k=1}^n 8\left(\frac12\right)^{k-1}.
\]

计算得

\[
P_n=8^n\left(\frac12\right)^{0+1+\cdots+(n-1)}
=8^n\left(\frac12\right)^{\frac{n(n-1)}2}.
\]

化为以 \(2\) 为底：

\[
P_n=2^{3n}\cdot 2^{-\frac{n(n-1)}2}
=2^{\frac{-n^2+7n}{2}}
=2^{\frac{n(7-n)}2}.
\]

因为 \(n\) 为正整数，要使 \(P_n\) 最大，只需使指数

\[
\frac{n(7-n)}2
\]

最大。该二次式在 \(n=3\) 或 \(n=4\) 时取最大值：

\[
\frac{3(7-3)}2=6,
\qquad
\frac{4(7-4)}2=6.
\]

所以

\[
P_{\max}=2^6=64.
\]

因此，\(a_1a_2\cdots a_n\) 的最大值为

\[
\boxed{64}
\]
